attributes.references: CMS NPI Registry; HIPAA Administrative Simplification 45 CFR Part 162; Health Level Seven (HL7) FHIR R4 Practitioner.identifier

attributes.name: payer_enrollment_status
attributes.description: Status of the provider's enrollment with payers under this organizational affiliation (group billing). Determines whether claims can be submitted under the organization's group NPI for this provider. Managed via Symplr Provider Enrollment.
attributes.references: CMS Provider Enrollment 42 CFR 424; Symplr Provider Enrollment; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: privileging_status
attributes.description: Current clinical privileging status for this provider at the affiliated organization. Clinical privileges define the specific procedures and services the provider is authorized to perform. Distinct from credentialing status.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.06.01.03; CMS Conditions of Participation 42 CFR 482.22; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this group membership record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance with HIPAA record retention requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR 164.312; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF; SOC 2

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this group membership record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and incremental ETL processing in the Databricks Lakehouse silver layer.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR 164.312; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF; SOC 2

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this affiliation record was sourced (e.g., Symplr Credentialing, Epic, Workday HCM). Supports data lineage, ETL reconciliation, and audit traceability.
attributes.references: HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; NIST Cybersecurity Framework; SOC 2

attributes.name: source_system_record_reference
attributes.description: The native identifier of this affiliation record in the originating operational system (e.g., Symplr provider affiliation ID, Epic provider record ID). Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the system of record.
attributes.references: HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; NIST Cybersecurity Framework; SOC 2

attributes.name: supervision_level
attributes.description: The level of supervision required for the provider under this organizational affiliation. Relevant for advanced practice providers (NPs, PAs) whose scope of practice may require physician oversight per state law and organizational policy.
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation; State Medical Practice Acts; The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.06.01.03; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: tax_identification_number
attributes.description: The federal Tax Identification Number (Employer Identification Number or Social Security Number) used for billing and tax reporting under this organizational affiliation. Required for claims submission and IRS 1099 reporting.
attributes.references: IRS Tax Reporting Requirements; CMS Provider Enrollment 42 CFR 424; HIPAA Administrative Simplification

attributes.name: verified_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the credentialing staff member or system that performed the primary source verification of this affiliation record. Required for credentialing audit trail per NCQA and Joint Commission standards.
attributes.references: NCQA Credentialing Standards Section 5; The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.06.01.03; Symplr Credentialing

attributes.name: verified_date
attributes.description: The date on which the affiliation or employment information was last verified through primary source verification as required by NCQA and The Joint Commission credentialing standards. Tracks compliance with mandatory verification timelines.
attributes.references: NCQA Credentialing Standards Section 5; The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.06.01.03; Symplr Credentialing

products.name: malpractice_coverage
products.description: Tracks professional liability (malpractice) insurance coverage for individual clinicians. Captures insurer name, policy number, coverage type (occurrence vs. claims-made), per-occurrence limit, aggregate limit, effective and expiration dates, tail coverage indicator, and coverage status. Required for credentialing verification and Joint Commission compliance.
products.reference: Joint Commission EC.02.01.01, State Medical Board Requirements

attributes.name: malpractice_coverage_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each malpractice (professional liability) insurance coverage record in the system. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; Symplr Credentialing

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the healthcare facility or organization at which this malpractice coverage is required for privileging purposes. A provider may have separate coverage records for different facilities within a health system.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; CMS Conditions of Participation; Symplr Credentialing

attributes.name: clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the licensed healthcare professional (physician, nurse practitioner, PA, etc.) for whom this malpractice coverage is maintained. Links to the provider master record.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; Symplr Credentialing; CMS Provider Enrollment

attributes.name: group_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to provider.group. Business justification: The malpractice_coverage table has a group_policy_indicator (BOOLEAN) field indicating that some malpractice policies are group-level policies covering multiple clinicians under a medical group. When

attributes.name: specialty_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to provider.specialty. Business justification: The malpractice_coverage table has a coverage_specialty (STRING) attribute that stores the specialty context of the malpractice policy as a free-text string. This is a denormalized reference to the sp

attributes.name: aggregate_limit
attributes.description: The maximum total dollar amount the insurer will pay for all malpractice claims during the policy period. Expressed in USD. Typically expressed as the second number in a coverage limit pair (e.g., $1M/$3M means $1M per occurrence, $3M aggregate).
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; State Departments of Health

attributes.name: certificate_of_insurance_url
attributes.description: URL or document management system path to the scanned or electronic Certificate of Insurance (COI) issued by the insurer. Stored as evidence of coverage for credentialing file documentation requirements.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; HIPAA Security Rule; ISO 27001

attributes.name: claims_history_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the provider has any reported malpractice claims or settlements associated with this policy period. Triggers additional review by the medical staff office and credentialing committee.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; OIG — Fraud and Abuse

attributes.name: coverage_lapse_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether there was a gap or lapse in malpractice coverage for this provider. A coverage lapse may affect hospital privileges, payer enrollment, and credentialing status and must be documented and explained.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: coverage_state
attributes.description: The U.S. state(s) in which this malpractice policy provides coverage, expressed as a two-letter USPS state abbreviation. Malpractice coverage is often state-specific; providers practicing in multiple states may require separate policies.
attributes.references: State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: coverage_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the malpractice insurance coverage record. 'Active' indicates the policy is in force and valid for credentialing purposes. Used by credentialing staff to determine whether a provider's coverage is current and compliant.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; Symplr Credentialing

attributes.name: coverage_type
attributes.description: Indicates the type of professional liability policy structure. 'Occurrence' covers incidents that occur during the policy period regardless of when the claim is filed. 'Claims-made' covers claims filed while the policy is active. 'Claims-made with tail' includes extended reporting endorsement. 'Nose coverage' (prior acts) covers incidents before the current policy start. 'Hybrid' combines elements of both.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; State Departments of Health

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this malpractice coverage record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and compliance reporting purposes.
attributes.references: HIPAA Security Rule; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF; The Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the monetary limits expressed in this coverage record (e.g., USD). Required for multi-entity health systems operating across international jurisdictions.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 — Currency Codes; GAAP and FASB — Financial Reporting Standards

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the malpractice insurance policy becomes effective and coverage begins. Used to determine whether a provider was covered during a specific period for credentialing and claims adjudication purposes.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which the malpractice insurance policy expires and coverage ends. Credentialing teams use this date to trigger renewal workflows and ensure continuous coverage compliance per Joint Commission standards.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: group_policy_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this coverage is provided under a group or organizational malpractice policy (e.g., hospital-sponsored coverage) rather than an individual policy purchased by the provider. Affects credentialing verification workflows.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; Symplr Credentialing

attributes.name: insurer_contact_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary contact person at the insurance carrier for verification and claims inquiries related to this policy. Used by credentialing staff during primary source verification (PSV).
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: insurer_contact_phone
attributes.description: Phone number for the insurance carrier's verification or credentialing department. Used by credentialing staff to conduct primary source verification (PSV) of coverage details.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: insurer_naic_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Insurer National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) Code
attributes.description: Five-digit National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) company code uniquely identifying the insurance carrier. Used for regulatory verification and insurer financial stability assessment.
attributes.references: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC); State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing

attributes.name: lapse_explanation
attributes.description: Free-text explanation documenting the reason for any gap or lapse in malpractice coverage. Required by credentialing committees when coverage_lapse_indicator is True. Applicable only when coverage_lapse_indicator is True.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: nose_coverage_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the policy includes prior acts (nose) coverage, which extends protection to incidents that occurred before the current policy's effective date. Relevant when a provider transitions between employers or insurers.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for credentialing staff to capture additional context, exceptions, or special conditions related to this malpractice coverage record that are not captured in structured fields (e.g., coverage exclusions, special endorsements, committee decisions).
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: open_claims_count
attributes.description: The number of currently open or pending malpractice claims against the provider under this policy. Used by credentialing committees to assess provider risk profile during initial credentialing and re-credentialing.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; OIG — Fraud and Abuse

attributes.name: per_occurrence_limit
attributes.description: The maximum dollar amount the insurer will pay for a single malpractice claim or incident. Expressed in USD. Credentialing bodies and hospital medical staff offices verify this meets minimum thresholds (e.g., $1,000,000 per occurrence).
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; State Departments of Health

attributes.name: policy_holder_name
attributes.description: The legal name of the named insured on the malpractice policy. This may be the individual provider, a group practice, or a healthcare organization. Used to confirm the provider is the named insured or an additional insured.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: policy_number
attributes.description: The externally-assigned unique identifier issued by the malpractice insurer for this professional liability policy. Used for verification during credentialing and payer enrollment processes.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; Symplr Credentialing

attributes.name: prior_acts_date
attributes.description: The retroactive date from which prior acts (nose) coverage applies. Incidents occurring on or after this date are covered under the current policy even if they predate the policy effective date. Applicable only when nose_coverage_indicator is True.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: renewal_reminder_date
attributes.description: The date on which the credentialing team should initiate the policy renewal workflow to ensure continuous coverage without lapse. Typically set a configurable number of days before the expiration date.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; Symplr Credentialing

attributes.name: self_insured_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the provider or their employing organization is self-insured for professional liability rather than carrying a commercial malpractice policy. Self-insured entities must demonstrate adequate reserves to meet credentialing requirements.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; State Departments of Health

attributes.name: source_record_reference
attributes.description: The native identifier of this malpractice coverage record in the originating operational system (e.g., Symplr record ID). Used for data lineage, deduplication, and reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver layer and source systems.
attributes.references: HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; NIST Cybersecurity Framework

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this malpractice coverage record was sourced (e.g., Symplr Credentialing, Epic, Cerner, MEDITECH, or manual entry). Used for data lineage and reconciliation in the Silver layer.
attributes.references: HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; NIST Cybersecurity Framework

attributes.name: tail_coverage_effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the extended reporting period (tail coverage) endorsement becomes effective, typically coinciding with the expiration of the underlying claims-made policy. Applicable only when tail_coverage_indicator is True.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: tail_coverage_expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which the extended reporting period (tail coverage) endorsement expires. After this date, no new claims can be reported under the tail endorsement. Applicable only when tail_coverage_indicator is True.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: tail_coverage_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether an extended reporting period (tail coverage) endorsement is in place for this claims-made policy. Tail coverage protects against claims filed after the policy expires for incidents that occurred during the policy period. Critical for credentialing continuity when a provider changes employers or retires.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this malpractice coverage record was last modified. Used for change tracking, audit trail, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver layer.
attributes.references: HIPAA Security Rule; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF; The Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: verification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the malpractice coverage was last verified through primary source verification (PSV) with the insurer. Required by The Joint Commission and NCQA for credentialing compliance.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; Symplr Credentialing

attributes.name: verification_method
attributes.description: The method used to perform primary source verification (PSV) of this malpractice coverage. Credentialing standards require documentation of how verification was obtained.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: verification_status
attributes.description: Indicates the primary source verification (PSV) status of this malpractice coverage record. 'Verified' means the coverage has been confirmed directly with the insurer. 'Pending' means verification is in progress. 'Failed' means verification could not be completed. 'Waived' means verification was waived per credentialing policy.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; Symplr Credentialing

attributes.name: verified_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the credentialing staff member or automated system that performed the primary source verification (PSV) of this malpractice coverage record.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) — Hospital Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards; Symplr Credentialing

products.name: dea_registration
products.description: Master record of DEA (Drug Enforcement Administration) controlled substance registrations for clinicians authorized to prescribe Schedule II-V medications. Captures DEA number, registration date, expiration date, DEA schedule authorizations, state of registration, registration status, and business activity type. Required for pharmacy order validation and controlled substance compliance.
products.reference: DEA Controlled Substances Act, 21 CFR Part 1301

attributes.name: dea_registration_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each DEA controlled substance registration record in the enterprise data platform. Primary key for the dea_registration data product.

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary healthcare facility or practice location associated with this DEA registration. DEA registrations are location-specific; this links the registration to the enterprise facility master record for network and compliance reporting.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; Joint Commission Credentialing Standards

attributes.name: clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the licensed healthcare professional or organizational provider who holds this DEA registration. Links to the authoritative provider master record.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301; NPI Registry — CMS

attributes.name: npi_registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.npi_registry. Business justification: DEA registration verification cross-references the NPI registry to confirm provider identity, enrollment status, and practice address during DEA application and renewal workflows. CMS and state PDMP p

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: DEA registrations create specific regulatory obligations (PDMP reporting, schedule II record-keeping, biennial inventory). The obligation entity tracks these regulatory requirements with due dates and

attributes.name: program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_program. Business justification: DEA registrations are governed by controlled substance compliance programs (PDMP compliance, DEA diversion prevention programs). The dea_registration.pdmp_reporting_required flag indicates program-lev

attributes.name: business_activity_type
attributes.description: The DEA-defined category of business activity for which the registration is issued. Determines the type of controlled substance activities the registrant is authorized to perform. Practitioner covers physicians, dentists, and veterinarians; mid-level practitioner covers nurse practitioners and physician assistants; hospital and pharmacy cover institutional registrants. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: practitioner|mid-level_practitioner|hospital|pharmacy|researcher|manufacturer|distributor|importer|exporter|reverse_distributor|narcotic_treatment_program — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.13; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: days_until_expiration
attributes.description: The number of calendar days remaining until the DEA registration expires, calculated as of the most recent data refresh date. Supports proactive credentialing management and pharmacy compliance dashboards. Note: This is a point-in-time snapshot value loaded during ETL; it is not a real-time computed field.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.31; Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

attributes.name: dea_number
attributes.description: The official DEA registration number assigned by the Drug Enforcement Administration to authorize the registrant to handle controlled substances. Format: two-letter prefix followed by seven digits. Used for pharmacy order validation and controlled substance prescribing verification.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.13; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: expiration_alert_date
attributes.description: The date on which the expiration alert notification was sent to the provider and/or credentialing staff. Null if no alert has been sent. Used for credentialing workflow audit trails.
attributes.references: Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; Internal Credentialing Policy

attributes.name: expiration_alert_sent
attributes.description: Indicates whether an expiration alert notification has been sent to the provider and/or credentialing staff regarding the upcoming expiration of this DEA registration. Supports proactive renewal workflow management.
attributes.references: Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; Internal Credentialing Policy

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the DEA registration expires and the provider is no longer authorized to prescribe or handle controlled substances under this registration. DEA registrations are typically issued for a three-year term. Critical for pharmacy order validation and compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.13; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: fee_amount
attributes.description: The registration fee paid to the DEA for the current registration period, in U.S. dollars. DEA registration fees vary by registrant type and are set by federal regulation. Used for credentialing cost tracking and budget reconciliation.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.21; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: fee_exempt
attributes.description: Indicates whether the registrant is exempt from DEA registration fees. Fee exemptions apply to federal, state, and local government practitioners, as well as certain public health service providers. Relevant for registration cost tracking and compliance.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.21; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for credentialing staff to document additional context, exceptions, or administrative notes related to the DEA registration. Examples include documentation of DEA correspondence, special conditions, or manual verification notes.
attributes.references: Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; Internal Credentialing Policy

attributes.name: payment_date
attributes.description: The date on which the DEA registration fee was paid for the current registration period. Used for financial reconciliation and credentialing audit trails.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.21; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: pdmp_reporting_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) Reporting Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the provider holding this DEA registration is subject to mandatory Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) reporting requirements in the registered state. PDMP reporting obligations vary by state and practitioner type.
attributes.references: State PDMP Statutes; PDMP TTAC (Training and Technical Assistance Center); DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: practitioner_type_code
attributes.description: DEA-assigned code identifying the specific practitioner type category (e.g., MD, DO, DDS, DVM, NP, PA, CRNA). Determines prescribing authority scope and schedule authorization eligibility. Sourced from DEA registration application form. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MD|DO|DDS|DMD|DVM|NP|PA|CRNA|CNM|PharmD|RPh|ND|OD|DPM|PhD — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1300.01; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this DEA registration record was first created in the enterprise data platform. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and compliance reporting requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164.312; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this DEA registration record was most recently updated in the enterprise data platform. Used for change tracking, incremental ETL processing, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164.312; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

attributes.name: registered_address_line1
attributes.description: Primary street address line of the practice location registered with the DEA. The DEA registration is location-specific; a provider with multiple practice sites may require separate registrations per location.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: registered_address_line2
attributes.description: Secondary address line (suite, floor, unit number) of the practice location registered with the DEA. Supplements the primary address line for precise location identification.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: registered_city
attributes.description: City of the practice location registered with the DEA for this controlled substance registration.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: registered_name
attributes.description: The full legal name of the individual practitioner or organization as it appears on the DEA registration certificate. May differ from the provider's operational display name. Used for verification against DEA public registry and pharmacy dispensing records.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.13; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: registered_zip_code
attributes.description: U.S. ZIP or ZIP+4 postal code of the practice location registered with the DEA. Used for geographic analysis of controlled substance prescribing patterns and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; USPS Postal Standards

attributes.name: registration_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the DEA registration was originally issued or most recently renewed by the Drug Enforcement Administration. Represents the effective start of the current registration period.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.13; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: registration_state
attributes.description: The U.S. state or territory in which the DEA registration is valid and the provider is authorized to prescribe controlled substances. DEA registrations are state-specific; a provider practicing in multiple states requires a separate DEA registration for each state. Represented as a two-letter USPS state abbreviation.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: registration_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the DEA registration. Active indicates the registration is valid and the provider may prescribe controlled substances. Expired indicates the registration has lapsed and must be renewed before prescribing. Suspended or revoked indicates regulatory action has been taken.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.36; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: registration_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DEA registration is held by an individual practitioner or by an institutional entity (e.g., hospital, clinic, pharmacy). Institutional registrations cover all authorized practitioners operating under the institution's DEA number.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: renewal_application_date
attributes.description: The date on which the provider submitted a renewal application to the DEA for continuation of the controlled substance registration. DEA regulations require renewal applications to be submitted at least 45 days before expiration. Used for credentialing workflow tracking in Symplr.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.31; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: renewal_confirmation_number
attributes.description: The confirmation or tracking number issued by the DEA upon receipt of a renewal application. Used to track the status of pending renewals and follow up with the DEA Diversion Control Division.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.31; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: revocation_date
attributes.description: The date on which the DEA registration was formally revoked by the Drug Enforcement Administration. Revocation is a permanent action distinct from suspension. Null when the registration has not been revoked.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.36; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: schedule_ii_authorized
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DEA registration authorizes the provider to prescribe Schedule II controlled substances (e.g., opioids such as oxycodone, stimulants such as amphetamine). Schedule II substances have high abuse potential with severe psychological or physical dependence. Required for CPOE validation in Epic Willow and Cerner PharmNet.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308.12; Controlled Substances Act

attributes.name: schedule_iii_authorized
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DEA registration authorizes the provider to prescribe Schedule III controlled substances (e.g., anabolic steroids, buprenorphine combinations). Schedule III substances have moderate to low physical dependence potential.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308.13; Controlled Substances Act

attributes.name: schedule_iin_authorized
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DEA registration authorizes the provider to prescribe Schedule IIN non-narcotic controlled substances (e.g., stimulants such as methylphenidate, Adderall). Distinct from Schedule IIN narcotic authorizations for pharmacy dispensing and order validation purposes.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308.12; Controlled Substances Act

attributes.name: schedule_iv_authorized
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DEA registration authorizes the provider to prescribe Schedule IV controlled substances (e.g., benzodiazepines, tramadol). Schedule IV substances have lower abuse potential relative to Schedule III.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308.14; Controlled Substances Act

attributes.name: schedule_v_authorized
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DEA registration authorizes the provider to prescribe Schedule V controlled substances (e.g., cough preparations with less than 200mg of codeine per 100mL). Schedule V substances have the lowest abuse potential among controlled substances.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308.15; Controlled Substances Act

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this DEA registration record was sourced or last updated. Supports data lineage tracking and ETL reconciliation across credentialing platforms.
attributes.references: HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; Internal Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: source_system_record_reference
attributes.description: The native record identifier for this DEA registration in the originating operational system (e.g., Symplr provider ID, Epic provider record number). Used for ETL reconciliation and cross-system traceability.
attributes.references: HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; Internal Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: surrender_date
attributes.description: The date on which the provider voluntarily surrendered the DEA registration to the Drug Enforcement Administration. Voluntary surrender may occur upon retirement, change of practice, or in lieu of revocation proceedings.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.52; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: suspension_date
attributes.description: The date on which the DEA registration was suspended by the Drug Enforcement Administration or voluntarily surrendered by the provider. Null when the registration has not been suspended. Triggers immediate pharmacy order blocking in CPOE systems.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.36; DEA Diversion Control Division

attributes.name: suspension_reason
attributes.description: Narrative description of the reason for suspension or revocation of the DEA registration, as documented by the DEA or the provider's credentialing department. Includes regulatory action codes, voluntary surrender reasons, or administrative hold explanations.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.36; OIG Exclusion Database

attributes.name: verification_date

products.name: affiliation
products.description: This association product represents the affiliation relationship between clinicians and organizational units within the healthcare workforce structure. It captures the many-to-many relationship where clinicians can hold appointments across multiple departments, divisions, or service lines, and each organizational unit has multiple affiliated clinicians. Each record links one clinician to one org unit with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific affiliation: FTE allocation percentage, affiliation type (primary, courtesy, consulting), medical staff category, and temporal validity dates. This is the operational system of record for clinician-department affiliations as managed jointly between Epic EHR provider master and Workday HCM organizational assignments.. Existence Justification: In healthcare operations, clinicians routinely hold appointments across multiple organizational units simultaneously. A cardiologist may have a primary affiliation with the Cardiology department (80% FTE), a courtesy affiliation with the ICU (15% FTE), and a consulting affiliation with the Cardiac Catheterization Lab (5% FTE). Each affiliation carries distinct attributes: FTE allocation percentage, affiliation type (primary/courtesy/consulting), medical staff category per department, and temporal validity dates. This is the 'Department Affiliation' business concept actively managed by medical staff offices and credentialing teams.

products.name: location_specialty
products.description: This association product represents the operational credential and directory record linking a provider practice location to a recognized medical specialty. It captures which specialties are offered at each location, which is the primary specialty, the active period of the offering, and whether the pairing is published to the provider directory. Each record is actively managed by credentialing and network management teams and is required for CMS provider enrollment, network adequacy reporting, and provider directory publishing compliance.. Existence Justification: In healthcare provider directory management, a single practice location routinely offers services across multiple specialties (e.g., a multi-specialty clinic offering cardiology, orthopedics, and internal medicine at one address), and a single specialty (e.g., Internal Medicine) is practiced at many different locations across a health system. This is an operationally managed relationship: credentialing teams actively create, update, and terminate location-specialty pairings as providers join, leave, or change their practice scope at a given site. The relationship carries its own business data — primary specialty designation, effective/termination dates, and directory publication status — that cannot reside on either parent entity alone.

attributes.name: body_site

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Coded reason for procedure cancellation when procedure_status is 'cancelled' or 'not-done'. attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; The Joint Commission OP.06.01.01; AHRQ Patient Safety Indicators

attributes.name: cdm_code
attributes.description: Internal facility CDM (Charge Description Master) code identifying the specific charge item for this procedure. Links clinical documentation to the revenue cycle charge capture process.
attributes.references: CDM (Charge Description Master); Epic Resolute HB; Cerner Revenue Cycle; CMS Charge Transparency Rule

attributes.name: charge_amount
attributes.description: Gross charge amount in USD posted to the patient account for this procedure, sourced from the CDM (Charge Description Master). Represents the facility's list price before contractual adjustments. Used for revenue cycle charge capture reconciliation.

attributes.name: consent_obtained
attributes.description: Indicates whether documented informed consent was obtained from the patient or authorized representative prior to the procedure. Required for regulatory compliance, medical-legal documentation, and The Joint Commission RI.01.03.01.

attributes.name: cpt_modifier_1
attributes.description: Primary AMA CPT modifier appended to the procedure code to indicate special circumstances (e.g., 22=Increased Procedural Services, 50=Bilateral, 51=Multiple Procedures, 59=Distinct Procedural Service). Required for accurate claim adjudication.
attributes.references: AMA CPT Modifier Guidelines; CMS-1500 Box 24D; CMS Claims Processing Manual Chapter 12

attributes.name: cpt_modifier_2
attributes.description: Secondary AMA CPT modifier when multiple modifiers are required for the procedure code. Supports complex claim scenarios such as assistant surgeon (80), teaching physician (GC), or anesthesia qualifiers.
attributes.references: AMA CPT Modifier Guidelines; CMS-1500 Box 24D; CMS Claims Processing Manual Chapter 12

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this procedure event record was first created in the source EHR system. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED field for data governance, audit trail, and HIPAA audit log requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA §164.312(b) Audit Controls; HITRUST CSF Control 09.aa; ISO 27001 A.12.4

attributes.name: duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total elapsed time in minutes from procedure start to procedure end. Derived from start and end timestamps at source and stored for OR utilization analytics, anesthesia billing, and surgical quality benchmarking.
attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; AHRQ OR Utilization Metrics

attributes.name: estimated_blood_loss_ml
attributes.description: Estimated blood loss in milliliters recorded by the surgical team during the procedure. Used for post-operative care planning, transfusion trigger assessment, and surgical quality benchmarking (ACS NSQIP).

attributes.name: icd10_pcs_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision Procedure Coding System (ICD-10-PCS) Code

attributes.name: laterality
attributes.description: Body side on which the procedure was performed. Required for surgical safety verification (Universal Protocol), correct-site surgery compliance, and ICD-10-PCS/CPT modifier application.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Clinical urgency classification of the procedure at time of scheduling or ordering. Drives OR scheduling queue prioritization, resource allocation, and EMTALA compliance tracking for emergent cases.

attributes.name: procedure_category
attributes.description: High-level clinical category classifying the nature of the procedure. Used for service-line analytics, OR scheduling resource allocation, and population health stratification.

attributes.name: procedure_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the procedure was performed. Used as the primary date dimension for reporting, HEDIS measure denominator logic, and claim date-of-service on CMS-1500 and UB-04 forms.

attributes.name: procedure_end_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the procedure was completed (wound closure for surgical cases, or final intervention for non-surgical). Used with start time to calculate procedure duration for OR scheduling, staffing, and quality metrics.

attributes.name: procedure_number

attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.identifier

attributes.name: procedure_start_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the procedure was initiated (knife-to-skin for surgical cases, or first intervention for non-surgical). Principal BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP for this transaction. Used for OR utilization, LOS calculation, and quality measure timing.
attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.performed[x]; The Joint Commission PC.01.02.01

attributes.name: procedure_status

attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.status; Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet

attributes.name: procedure_type
attributes.description: Operational classification of the procedure within the facility's CDM (Charge Description Master), such as 'OR Case', 'Bedside Procedure', 'Interventional Radiology', 'Endoscopy', 'Cardiac Cath'. Drives charge routing and scheduling resource assignment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: or_case|bedside|interventional_radiology|endoscopy|cardiac_cath|ambulatory_surgery|labor_delivery — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; CDM (Charge Description Master); CMS Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS)

attributes.name: source_system

attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001 Data Lineage

attributes.name: specimen_collected
attributes.description: Indicates whether a tissue specimen or pathology sample was collected during the procedure. Triggers downstream laboratory/pathology order workflow and chain-of-custody documentation.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this procedure event record in the source EHR system. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED field for change data capture (CDC), data quality monitoring, and HIPAA audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: HIPAA §164.312(b) Audit Controls; HITRUST CSF Control 09.aa; ISO 27001 A.12.4; HL7 FHIR R4 Meta.lastUpdated

products.name: vital_sign
products.description: Patient vital sign measurements captured during clinical encounters, nursing assessments, and continuous monitoring. Includes LOINC-coded observation types: blood pressure (systolic/diastolic), heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature, SpO2, height, weight, BMI, pain score, and Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS). Captures measured value, unit of measure, measurement method, body site, patient position, device used, measurement date/time, and recording clinician. Supports early warning score (EWS/MEWS/NEWS) calculations, sepsis screening, and clinical deterioration detection. High-volume time-series clinical data sourced from Epic ClinDoc flowsheets, Cerner PowerChart, and bedside monitoring device integrations. Separated from clinical_observation due to distinct high-frequency time-series ingestion patterns, dedicated device integration pipelines, and specialized analytics (trending, alerting, waveform correlation). Maps to FHIR Observation with vitals profile (US Core Vital Signs).

products.name: observation
products.description: SSOT for all structured clinical observations, assessments, scored evaluations, and clinical findings documented by clinicians during patient care. Encompasses LOINC-coded and SNOMED CT-coded observations across all clinical contexts including: nursing assessments (head-to-toe, skin integrity, restraint, fall risk using Morse/Braden scales, pressure injury staging, discharge readiness), functional status assessments (Barthel Index, FIM, ADL/IADL), behavioral health screenings (PHQ-9, CAGE-AID, Columbia Suicide Severity), SDOH screenings, wound assessments, intake/output measurements, neurological assessments (GCS components), physical examination findings, symptom documentation, and clinical impressions. Captures observation code, value (numeric, coded, or text), units, reference range, interpretation flag (normal, abnormal, critical), observation_category (nursing, functional, finding, screening, exam), assessment tool used, body system/site, laterality, severity, presence status (present, absent, unknown), observation date/time, and recording clinician. High-volume structured clinical data sourced from Epic ClinDoc flowsheets, Cerner PowerChart, and structured documentation modules. Supports nursing quality metrics, discharge planning, population health stratification, Joint Commission compliance, and FHIR Observation resource interoperability.

products.name: care_plan
products.description: Patient-centered care plans documenting clinical goals, interventions, and expected outcomes across the care continuum. Captures care plan type (inpatient, outpatient, chronic disease, discharge, transitional), status (draft, active, completed, revoked), effective date range, care setting, authoring provider, care team assignment, patient goals with individual lifecycle tracking, clinical problems addressed, and care plan category (SNOMED CT coded). Includes embedded care plan goals as detail records: goal description, SNOMED CT coded goal category, target measure (LOINC coded), target value, target date, achievement status (proposed, accepted, in-progress, achieved, cancelled), priority, and responsible provider. Supports transitions of care, population health management, ACO care coordination, and CMS Conditions of Participation for discharge planning. Sourced from Epic Healthy Planet and Cerner.

products.name: care_team

Distinct from workforce scheduling — this is the clinical accountability record. Enables care coordination queries, transitions of care documentation, and care plan team assignment. attributes.description: Indicates whether this care team member is currently designated as on-call for the patient. On-call designation determines who is contacted for urgent clinical decisions outside of normal coverage hours.

attributes.name: is_primary_contact

attributes.name: member_role_code

attributes.name: member_start_date

attributes.name: sdoh_flag

products.name: advance_directive
products.description: Patient advance directive and end-of-life care preference documentation including DNR (Do Not Resuscitate) orders, POLST/MOLST (Physician/Medical Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment), living wills, healthcare power of attorney designations, and code status (Full Code, DNR, DNR/DNI, Comfort Care). Captures directive type, effective date, expiration date, document status (active, revoked, superseded), healthcare proxy name and contact information, verification method, and the provider who documented or verified the directive. domains.name: order
domains.description: Manages the full lifecycle of clinical orders including CPOE (Computerized Physician Order Entry) for lab, radiology, pharmacy, and referral orders. Tracks order status, priority, routing, and fulfillment. Integrates with Epic Orders, Beaker (LIS), Radiant (RIS), and Willow (pharmacy) as the operational order management backbone.

products.name: clinical_order
products.description: Core master record for every clinical order entered via CPOE (Computerized Physician Order Entry) in Epic Orders or Cerner Millennium. Captures the authoritative order identity, ordering provider NPI, patient MRN, order type (lab, radiology, pharmacy, referral, nursing, dietary, consult), order priority (STAT, routine, urgent, timed), order mode (verbal, written, electronic), clinical indication (ICD-10 coded), ordering datetime, start and stop datetimes, order source system, order set membership flag, parent order reference for linked/chained orders, current order status, and order class (inpatient, outpatient, ED, ambulatory). SSOT for all clinical order identity, metadata, and type/priority classification across the enterprise. Absorbs order_type and order_priority reference attributes as embedded enums. All modality-specific attributes are owned by extension products (lab_order, radiology_order, pharmacy_order, referral_order).

attributes.name: cds_alert_overridden
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinical Decision Support (CDS) Alert Overridden Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Clinical Decision Support (CDS) alert was overridden by the provider when this event was triggered. True = alert was acknowledged and overridden; False = alert was not overridden or no alert was present. Critical for patient safety audit and alert override rate reporting.
attributes.references: ONC 21st Century Cures Act; AHRQ Patient Safety; Joint Commission NPSG

attributes.name: cosignature_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this order modification or event requires a co-signature from a supervising or authorizing provider before the change takes effect. Applies to resident/trainee orders and controlled substance modifications per institutional policy.
attributes.references: Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.24; DEA 21 CFR Part 1306

attributes.name: cosignature_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the required co-signature was completed by the supervising provider. Null if co-signature has not yet been obtained. Used to measure co-signature turnaround time for compliance reporting.
attributes.references: Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.24

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this history record was first written to the lakehouse silver layer. Represents the ETL ingestion time, distinct from event_timestamp (the real-world clinical event time). Used for data pipeline monitoring and late-arrival detection.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; HITRUST CSF; Data Lineage Standards

attributes.name: dea_schedule
attributes.description: The DEA controlled substance schedule (CI through CV) applicable to the medication order at the time of this event. Populated only when is_controlled_substance is True. Determines regulatory handling requirements.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308; Controlled Substances Act

attributes.name: discontinuation_type
attributes.description: Classifies the reason category for order discontinuation when event_type is DISCONTINUATION. AMA = Against Medical Advice. Supports medication reconciliation, discharge planning, and quality reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: COMPLETED|PROVIDER_DISCONTINUED|PATIENT_REFUSED|AMA|FORMULARY|DUPLICATE|PROTOCOL — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.statusReason; Joint Commission MM.04.01.01; AMA Guidelines

attributes.name: effective_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time at which this lifecycle event becomes clinically effective (e.g., when a renewed order becomes active, when a hold is lifted). May differ from event_timestamp when events are scheduled or backdated. Supports medication administration record (MAR) reconciliation.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.occurrenceDateTime; Epic Orders; MAR Standards

attributes.name: event_sequence_number
attributes.description: Monotonically increasing sequence number for all lifecycle events belonging to the same parent order. Enables chronological ordering of events within an order's history and detection of out-of-order event delivery from source systems.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 AuditEvent; Epic Orders Audit Log; Data Lineage Standards

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (with timezone offset) at which this lifecycle event occurred in the clinical system. This is the authoritative real-world event time, distinct from record audit timestamps. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); HL7 FHIR R4 AuditEvent.recorded

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Discriminator classifying the kind of lifecycle event recorded. STATUS_CHANGE = workflow state transition; MODIFICATION = dose/frequency/route/priority change; AMENDMENT = clinical content update; CORRECTION = error correction; RENEWAL = order re-authorization; DISCONTINUATION = order stopped; COSIGN_REQUEST = co-signature required; COSIGN_COMPLETED = co-signature fulfilled. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: STATUS_CHANGE|MODIFICATION|AMENDMENT|CORRECTION|RENEWAL|DISCONTINUATION|COSIGN_REQUEST|COSIGN_COMPLETED — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Task.status; Epic Orders Event Types; Joint Commission RC.02.01.01

attributes.name: hipaa_audit_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Audit Category
attributes.description: HIPAA-defined audit event category for this order lifecycle event, used for compliance reporting to OCR and internal privacy audits. Classifies the event as an access, modification, disclosure, correction, or deletion of PHI per HIPAA Security Rule requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); OCR Audit Protocol; HITRUST CSF Control 09.aa

attributes.name: is_amendment
attributes.description: Indicates whether this event represents a formal clinical amendment to the order record (as opposed to a routine status change or system-generated update). True = formal amendment requiring clinical documentation. Supports HIM and CDI amendment tracking.
attributes.references: Joint Commission RC.01.03.01; HIM Standards; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.526

attributes.name: is_controlled_substance
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order subject to this lifecycle event involves a DEA-scheduled controlled substance. True = controlled substance order. Triggers enhanced audit requirements and DEA compliance tracking.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1306; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); State Pharmacy Boards

attributes.name: is_verbal_order
attributes.description: Indicates whether this order event was initiated as a verbal or telephone order requiring subsequent written authentication. True = verbal/telephone order; False = directly entered CPOE order. Tracked for Joint Commission verbal order compliance.
attributes.references: Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.24(c)(1)(ii)

attributes.name: modified_field_name
attributes.description: The name of the specific clinical order field that was changed during a MODIFICATION, AMENDMENT, or CORRECTION event (e.g., 'dose', 'frequency', 'route', 'quantity', 'priority', 'start_date', 'stop_date', 'indication'). Null for pure status transitions.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Audit Log; Cerner Millennium Audit Trail; CDI Standards

attributes.name: modifying_user_role
attributes.description: The clinical or operational role of the user who triggered this lifecycle event at the time of the event. Supports role-based audit analysis and compliance review (e.g., identifying unauthorized order modifications). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PHYSICIAN|NURSE|PHARMACIST|RESIDENT|SYSTEM|ADMIN|TECHNICIAN — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(a)(1); Joint Commission; OIG Compliance

attributes.name: new_status
attributes.description: The order workflow status immediately after this lifecycle event. Together with previous_status, defines the state transition that occurred. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DRAFT|PENDING|ACTIVE|HOLD|SUSPENDED|COMPLETED|DISCONTINUED|CANCELLED|EXPIRED|ERROR — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.status; Epic Orders Status Codes

attributes.name: new_value
attributes.description: The value of the modified clinical field immediately after this modification event. Paired with previous_value to form a complete before/after audit record. Contains PHI when the field relates to medication or clinical details.
attributes.references: Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); CDI Standards

attributes.name: order_number
attributes.description: The human-readable, externally visible order identifier (e.g., Epic order number, Cerner accession number) at the time of this event. Denormalized from the order header to support direct lookup in audit reports without joining to the order table.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium; Joint Commission RC.01.02.01

attributes.name: order_priority
attributes.description: The priority level of the order at the time of this event. Captures the priority as it existed at this point in the lifecycle, enabling detection of priority escalations or de-escalations over time.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.priority; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Classification of the clinical order category at the time of this event. Determines routing to downstream fulfillment systems: LAB → Beaker/LIS; RADIOLOGY → Radiant/RIS; PHARMACY → Willow; REFERRAL → Cadence. Denormalized here to support event-level analytics without joining back to the order header. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: LAB|RADIOLOGY|PHARMACY|REFERRAL|PROCEDURE|NURSING|DIET|CONSULT — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.category; Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium

attributes.name: override_reason
attributes.description: The structured or free-text reason provided by the provider when overriding a Clinical Decision Support (CDS) alert associated with this order event. Populated only when cds_alert_overridden is True. Supports patient safety review and quality improvement programs.
attributes.references: ONC 21st Century Cures Act; AHRQ Patient Safety; Joint Commission NPSG.03.06.01

attributes.name: previous_status
attributes.description: The order workflow status immediately before this lifecycle event. Enables reconstruction of the full state machine history and supports CDI review and medication reconciliation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DRAFT|PENDING|ACTIVE|HOLD|SUSPENDED|COMPLETED|DISCONTINUED|CANCELLED|EXPIRED|ERROR — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.status; Epic Orders Status Codes

attributes.name: previous_value
attributes.description: The value of the modified clinical field (dose, frequency, route, priority, quantity, etc.) immediately before this modification event. Stored as a string to accommodate heterogeneous field types across order categories. Populated only for MODIFICATION, AMENDMENT, and CORRECTION event types. Contains PHI when the field relates to medication or clinical details.
attributes.references: Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); CDI Standards

attributes.name: reason_code
attributes.description: Structured reason code explaining why this lifecycle event occurred (e.g., CLINICAL_CHANGE, PATIENT_REQUEST, PROVIDER_CORRECTION, DUPLICATE_ORDER, ALLERGY_ALERT, DRUG_INTERACTION, FORMULARY_SUBSTITUTION, PROTOCOL_CHANGE). Sourced from the EHR reason code catalog. Supports CDI and quality review workflows.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.reasonCode; Epic Orders; Joint Commission

attributes.name: reason_text
attributes.description: Free-text clinical justification or narrative explanation provided by the user or system for this lifecycle event. Supplements the structured reason_code with provider-authored context. May contain PHI when clinical rationale references patient-specific information.
attributes.references: Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); CDI Standards

attributes.name: renewal_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential counter indicating which renewal iteration this event represents for the parent order. Starts at 1 for the first renewal. Null for non-renewal events. Supports chronic medication management and long-term order tracking.
attributes.references: Epic Willow; Cerner PharmNet; Joint Commission MM.04.01.01

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record that generated this lifecycle event. Identifies the originating EHR module for data lineage and reconciliation purposes (e.g., EPIC_ORDERS for physician CPOE, WILLOW for pharmacy verification, BEAKER for lab order processing, RADIANT for radiology order management). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EPIC_ORDERS|CERNER_POWERCHARTS|WILLOW|BEAKER|RADIANT|MEDITECH|MANUAL — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 AuditEvent.source; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

attributes.name: transmission_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time at which this order event was transmitted to the downstream fulfillment system (Beaker, Radiant, Willow, etc.). Null if transmission is not required or has not yet occurred.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Task.lastModified; Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium

attributes.name: transmission_status
attributes.description: Status of the order transmission to the downstream fulfillment system (pharmacy, lab, radiology) following this lifecycle event. Tracks whether the event was successfully communicated to the executing department.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Task.status; Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this history record was last updated in the lakehouse silver layer. Although the event log is intended to be immutable, this field captures any correction or reprocessing events applied to the record for data quality purposes.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; HITRUST CSF; Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: verbal_order_authentication_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time at which a verbal or telephone order was authenticated (signed) by the ordering provider. Null for non-verbal orders. Must occur within the timeframe required by Joint Commission standards (typically 24-48 hours).
attributes.references: Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.24(c)(1)(ii)

attributes.name: workstation_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the clinical workstation, device, or terminal from which this order lifecycle event was initiated. Supports HIPAA access audit trails and security incident investigation.

products.name: referral_order
products.description: Clinical order for patient referral to a specialist, external provider, or care program. Captures referring provider NPI, receiving provider NPI, specialty type, referral reason (ICD-10 coded), urgency level, authorization requirement flag, payer authorization number, referral expiration date, number of authorized visits, referral source (PCP, ED, inpatient), and referral disposition (accepted, declined, pending, completed). Integrates with Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management and payer authorization workflows.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to provider.provider_location. Business justification: Referral orders must specify the exact practice location where the patient will be seen for appointment scheduling, directory accuracy, and referral loop closure. provider_location captures site-speci

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.npi_registry. Business justification: referral_order.referring_provider_npi is a plain-text denormalization of the NPI Registry. Linking to npi_registry supports referral network credentialing validation, CMS referral quality reporting, a

attributes.name: specialty_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to provider.specialty. Business justification: Referral routing, network adequacy analysis, and payer authorization workflows require structured specialty linkage. Receiving_provider_clinician_id provides individual, but specialty_id enables speci

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical encounter or visit during which the referral order was initiated. Links to the encounter visit record.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Cadence; HL7 FHIR Encounter Resource

attributes.name: authorization_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the patient's payer requires prior authorization before the referral can be fulfilled. When True, the referral workflow is gated on obtaining a payer authorization number before scheduling.
attributes.references: CMS Prior Authorization Rules; Epic EHR Resolute PB; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; HIPAA 45 CFR §162

attributes.name: authorized_visits
attributes.description: The number of specialist visits or service encounters approved by the payer under this referral authorization. Used to track utilization against the authorized limit and trigger re-authorization workflows.
attributes.references: CMS Prior Authorization Rules; Epic EHR Resolute PB; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: The documented reason for cancellation of the referral order when order_status is 'cancelled'. Captures clinical, administrative, or patient-driven reasons for cancellation to support quality improvement and operational analytics.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Orders Module; Joint Commission; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management

attributes.name: clinical_indication
attributes.description: Structured or semi-structured clinical indication supporting the medical necessity of the referral. May include relevant findings, lab results, imaging results, or prior treatment history that justify the specialist consultation.
attributes.references: Epic EHR ClinDoc; Joint Commission Medical Necessity Documentation; CMS Medical Necessity Guidelines; HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.supportingInfo

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the referral order record was first created in the lakehouse Silver layer. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: disposition_date
attributes.description: The date on which the referral disposition was recorded by the receiving provider or care coordinator. Used to measure referral loop closure timeliness and time-to-specialist metrics.
attributes.references: Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; NCQA HEDIS; Epic EHR Orders Module

attributes.name: disposition_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes from the receiving provider or care coordinator documenting the reason for the referral disposition, particularly for declined or cancelled referrals. Supports clinical documentation improvement (CDI) and care coordination workflows.
attributes.references: Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; Epic EHR ClinDoc; Joint Commission Documentation Standards

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the referral authorization becomes valid and the patient may begin receiving referred services. Typically the date the authorization was approved by the payer.
attributes.references: CMS Prior Authorization Rules; Epic EHR Resolute PB; Salesforce Health Cloud

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date after which the referral authorization is no longer valid and services cannot be rendered under this referral. Triggers re-authorization workflows and patient outreach when approaching expiry.
attributes.references: CMS Prior Authorization Rules; Epic EHR Resolute PB; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management

attributes.name: first_available_date
attributes.description: The earliest available appointment date offered by the receiving provider at the time the referral was processed. Used to measure access to specialty care and network adequacy.
attributes.references: NCQA HEDIS Access and Availability Measures; CMS Network Adequacy Standards; Salesforce Health Cloud

attributes.name: is_stat_order
attributes.description: Indicates whether the referral order was placed as a STAT (immediate/urgent) order requiring expedited processing and scheduling. Distinct from urgency_level as this is the operational flag used by scheduling and authorization workflows.
attributes.references: Epic EHR CPOE; Joint Commission; EMTALA

attributes.name: loop_closed_date
attributes.description: The date on which the referral communication loop was closed, meaning the referring provider received the specialist's consultation report or outcome documentation.
attributes.references: NCQA HEDIS; NCQA PCMH Standards; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management

attributes.name: mrn
attributes.description: The patient's Medical Record Number (MRN) as assigned by the facility's Master Patient Index (MPI). Included on the referral for cross-system patient identification and payer submission.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; Epic EHR MPI; Joint Commission Patient Identification Standards

attributes.name: order_placed_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the referring provider placed the referral order via Computerized Physician Order Entry (CPOE) in the Electronic Health Record (EHR). This is the principal business event timestamp for the referral lifecycle.
attributes.references: Epic EHR CPOE; HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.authoredOn; Joint Commission Documentation Standards

attributes.name: order_source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which the referral order was originated or ingested into the lakehouse. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and multi-system integration auditing.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Orders Module; Salesforce Health Cloud; HL7 FHIR; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current workflow lifecycle state of the referral order. Drives downstream processing in Salesforce Health Cloud and Epic Orders. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|active|accepted|declined|completed|cancelled|expired — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Epic EHR Orders Module; HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.status; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management

attributes.name: plan_type
attributes.description: The type of health insurance plan governing the referral authorization requirements. HMO and POS plans typically require referrals; PPO plans may not. Drives authorization workflow logic. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: HMO|PPO|POS|EPO|Medicare|Medicaid|self_pay — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CMS; NCQA; Epic EHR Resolute PB; HIPAA 45 CFR §162

attributes.name: receiving_provider_npi
attributes.description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the specialist or receiving provider to whom the patient is referred. Required for payer authorization and claims adjudication.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Registry; HIPAA 45 CFR §162.406; CMS-1500; UB-04

attributes.name: referral_disposition
attributes.description: The outcome or final disposition of the referral as reported by the receiving provider. Indicates whether the specialist accepted, declined, completed, or the patient did not attend. Used for referral loop closure tracking and quality reporting.
attributes.references: Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; Epic EHR Orders Module; NCQA HEDIS; Joint Commission

attributes.name: referral_loop_closed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the referring provider has received and acknowledged the specialist's consultation report, closing the referral communication loop. A key quality metric for NCQA HEDIS and PCMH accreditation.
attributes.references: NCQA HEDIS; NCQA PCMH Standards; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; Epic EHR Healthy Planet

attributes.name: referral_number
attributes.description: Externally visible, human-readable business identifier for the referral order. Used in payer communications, patient correspondence, and cross-system tracking (e.g., Salesforce Health Cloud, Epic Orders). Format: REF- followed by 10 digits.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Orders Module; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; CMS-1500 Claim Form

attributes.name: referral_reason_description
attributes.description: Free-text clinical narrative describing the reason for the referral, supplementing the ICD-10 code. Captures clinical context not fully expressed by the diagnosis code, such as symptom progression, treatment failure, or specific clinical question for the specialist.
attributes.references: Epic EHR ClinDoc; Joint Commission Documentation Standards; HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.reasonCode

attributes.name: referral_source
attributes.description: The clinical setting or care context from which the referral originated. Indicates whether the referral was initiated by a Primary Care Physician (PCP), Emergency Department (ED), inpatient unit, specialist, patient self-referral, or care program enrollment.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Orders Module; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; NCQA HEDIS

attributes.name: referral_type
attributes.description: Categorizes the nature of the referral: to a specialist, external provider, care program, second opinion, or for a specific diagnostic workup. Used for operational routing and analytics segmentation.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Orders Module; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.category

attributes.name: scheduled_appointment_date
attributes.description: The date on which the patient's appointment with the receiving specialist or provider has been scheduled. Used to measure time-to-appointment and referral fulfillment timeliness.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Cadence; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; NCQA HEDIS Access and Availability Measures

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the referral order record was last modified in the lakehouse Silver layer. Supports change detection and incremental processing.

attributes.name: urgency_level
attributes.description: Clinical priority level assigned to the referral order by the referring provider. Drives scheduling priority at the receiving provider and payer authorization turnaround time requirements. Values: routine, urgent, stat, emergent.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Orders Module; HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.priority; Joint Commission; EMTALA

attributes.name: visits_used
attributes.description: The number of authorized visits that have been consumed against this referral to date. Compared against authorized_visits to determine remaining utilization and trigger re-authorization alerts.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Resolute PB; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; CMS Prior Authorization Rules

products.name: set
products.description: Master record for pre-defined, evidence-based bundles of clinical orders (order sets) and their governing clinical protocols and care pathways. Captures order set name, clinical indication, specialty, version number, effective and expiration dates, approval status, approving committee, evidence-based guideline reference, associated DRG or care pathway, active/inactive flag, protocol governance attributes (governance level — guideline, consensus, regulatory mandate), clinical condition or diagnosis trigger (ICD-10), applicable care setting, owning clinical department, evidence level, parent protocol hierarchy, and approval workflow status. SSOT for both the executable order bundle and the clinical policy that governs its activation. Managed in Epic Orders and Cerner Millennium.

attributes.description: Identifier of the physician or clinical leader who formally approved the order set on behalf of the approving committee. Supports governance accountability and regulatory audit requirements.
