attributes.description: Identifier of the clinician or clinical informaticist who originally authored and submitted the order set for governance review. Links to the provider master for accountability and audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HIPAA Security Rule; Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: specialty_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to provider.specialty. Business justification: Order sets are specialty-specific clinical protocols (cardiology admission order sets, oncology treatment pathways). Healthcare organizations maintain specialty-based order set libraries, track specia

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the approving clinical committee formally approved the current version of the order set. Establishes the official governance record for audit and regulatory reporting purposes.
attributes.references: Joint Commission (TJC); CMS Conditions of Participation; HIM Governance

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current approval workflow status of the order set within the clinical governance process. Drives whether the order set is available for provider use in CPOE. 'draft' = under development; 'pending_review' = submitted to approving committee; 'approved' = active and available; 'retired' = superseded; 'suspended' = temporarily withdrawn.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC); CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: approving_committee
attributes.description: Name of the clinical governance committee or body responsible for reviewing and approving the order set (e.g., 'Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee', 'Medical Executive Committee', 'Clinical Quality Council'). Required for Joint Commission accreditation and CMS Conditions of Participation compliance.
attributes.references: Joint Commission (TJC); CMS Conditions of Participation; Medical Staff Bylaws

attributes.name: care_pathway_name
attributes.description: Name of the clinical care pathway or protocol bundle with which this order set is associated (e.g., 'Sepsis Care Pathway', 'Hip Replacement Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) Pathway'). Links the executable order bundle to the broader clinical protocol framework.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC); AHRQ

attributes.name: care_setting
attributes.description: Clinical care setting in which the order set is intended to be used. Restricts order set availability to appropriate clinical contexts within the EHR. 'inpatient' = admitted patients; 'outpatient' = clinic/ambulatory; 'emergency' = Emergency Department (ED); 'icu' = Intensive Care Unit (ICU); 'surgical' = Operating Room (OR)/perioperative; 'observation' = observation status.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: clinical_indication
attributes.description: Free-text or structured description of the clinical condition, diagnosis, or scenario that triggers activation of this order set (e.g., 'Suspected sepsis with organ dysfunction', 'Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction'). Complements the ICD-10 trigger code.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; SNOMED CT; HL7 FHIR

attributes.name: compliance_rate_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of triggered clinical scenarios where the order set was activated by providers, as reported by the EHR analytics module. Sourced from Epic reporting or Cerner analytics — not computed in the lakehouse. Supports HEDIS, MIPS, and VBP quality measure reporting.
attributes.references: CMS MIPS; HEDIS; NCQA; VBP Program; Joint Commission (TJC) ORYX

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the order set record was first created in the source system or lakehouse. Supports audit trail requirements per HIPAA Security Rule, Joint Commission, and HIM governance policies.
attributes.references: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164); Joint Commission (TJC); HIM Governance

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the order set version becomes clinically effective and available for provider use in CPOE. Aligns with the approved go-live date established by the governing clinical committee.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: evidence_level
attributes.description: Strength of clinical evidence supporting the order set, using standard evidence grading. 'A' = strong evidence from multiple randomized controlled trials; 'B' = moderate evidence; 'C' = limited evidence; 'D' = very limited evidence; 'expert_consensus' = based on expert opinion in absence of trials. Supports quality measurement and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: AHRQ Evidence-Based Practice; NCQA; Joint Commission (TJC); ACC/AHA Evidence Classification

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the order set version expires and is no longer valid for clinical use. Null indicates no scheduled expiration. Triggers mandatory review workflow when approaching expiration per clinical governance policy.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC); NCQA

attributes.name: fhir_plan_definition_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) PlanDefinition ID
attributes.description: HL7 FHIR PlanDefinition resource identifier corresponding to this order set, enabling interoperability with Health Information Exchange (HIE) platforms and external clinical decision support systems. Aligns with HL7 FHIR R4 PlanDefinition resource.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 PlanDefinition; ONC 21st Century Cures Act; HIE Standards

attributes.name: governance_level
attributes.description: Classification of the governance authority underpinning the order set protocol. 'guideline' = based on published clinical practice guidelines; 'consensus' = based on institutional expert consensus without external guideline; 'regulatory_mandate' = required by CMS, Joint Commission, or other regulatory body (e.g., CMS Core Measures, EMTALA requirements).
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation; Joint Commission (TJC); OIG; AHRQ

attributes.name: guideline_reference
attributes.description: Citation or reference to the external clinical practice guideline, systematic review, or regulatory mandate that underpins the order set (e.g., 'Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 Guidelines', 'AHA/ACC STEMI Management Guidelines 2023', 'CMS Sepsis Core Measure SEP-1'). Supports clinical documentation improvement (CDI) and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: AHRQ; NCQA; CMS Core Measures; Joint Commission (TJC) ORYX; WHO

attributes.name: includes_lab_orders
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set bundle contains laboratory orders routed to Beaker (LIS) or equivalent Laboratory Information System (LIS). True = lab orders present; False = no lab orders included.

attributes.name: includes_pharmacy_orders
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set bundle contains medication orders routed to Willow (pharmacy) or equivalent pharmacy system. True = pharmacy/medication orders present; False = no pharmacy orders included. Relevant for DEA controlled substance tracking.
attributes.references: Epic Willow; Cerner PharmNet; DEA Controlled Substances; NDC Standards

attributes.name: includes_radiology_orders
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set bundle contains radiology/imaging orders routed to Radiant (RIS) or equivalent Radiology Information System (RIS). True = radiology orders present; False = no radiology orders included.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant (RIS); Cerner RadNet; PACS Standards

attributes.name: includes_referral_orders
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set bundle contains referral orders to specialists or ancillary services. True = referral orders present; False = no referral orders included. Supports care coordination and transitions of care workflows.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set is currently active and available for selection in the CPOE workflow. True = active and selectable by providers; False = inactive and hidden from the order entry interface. Distinct from approval_status — an approved order set may be temporarily deactivated without retiring it.

attributes.name: is_cms_core_measure
attributes.business_glossary_term: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Core Measure Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this order set is directly associated with a CMS Core Measure or quality reporting requirement (e.g., SEP-1 Sepsis Bundle, VTE Prophylaxis). True = linked to a CMS Core Measure; False = not a CMS Core Measure order set. Supports quality measurement and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: CMS Core Measures; Joint Commission (TJC) ORYX; AHRQ; VBP Program

attributes.name: is_hipaa_sensitive
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Sensitive Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set is associated with HIPAA-sensitive clinical categories requiring enhanced access controls (e.g., behavioral health, substance use disorder, HIV/AIDS, reproductive health). True = sensitive category requiring additional PHI protections; False = standard clinical order set.
attributes.references: HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164); 42 CFR Part 2 (Substance Use Disorder); OCR HIPAA Enforcement

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent clinical review of the order set, regardless of whether a version change resulted. Supports mandatory periodic review cycles (typically annual) required by Joint Commission and institutional policy.
attributes.references: Joint Commission (TJC); NCQA; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Date by which the next mandatory clinical review of the order set must be completed. Drives governance workflow alerts and ensures compliance with periodic review requirements per Joint Commission and institutional policy.
attributes.references: Joint Commission (TJC); NCQA; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: order_count
attributes.description: Total number of individual clinical orders (lab, radiology, pharmacy, nursing, referral) included in the order set bundle. Provides a quick indicator of order set complexity and scope for provider review.

attributes.name: order_set_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the order set within the source system (e.g., Epic Orders catalog ID or Cerner Millennium order set mnemonic). Used for cross-system referencing and integration with Beaker (LIS), Radiant (RIS), and Willow (pharmacy).

attributes.name: order_set_type
attributes.description: Classification of the order set by its clinical purpose in the care continuum. 'admission' = admission orders bundle; 'discharge' = discharge planning orders; 'procedure' = pre/intra/post-procedure orders; 'condition' = condition-specific management bundle; 'preventive' = preventive care protocol; 'transition' = transitions of care orders.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: owning_department
attributes.description: Name of the clinical department or service line that owns and is responsible for maintaining the order set (e.g., 'Department of Cardiology', 'Emergency Medicine', 'Pharmacy'). Establishes accountability for content governance and periodic review.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: population_age_group
attributes.description: Target patient age group for which the order set is clinically appropriate. Restricts order set availability to appropriate patient populations in CPOE. 'pediatric' = patients under 18; 'adult' = 18-64; 'geriatric' = 65+; 'neonatal' = newborns; 'all' = all age groups.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; AAP Pediatric Guidelines; CMS

attributes.name: renal_adjustment_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set contains medications requiring renal function-based dose adjustments (e.g., creatinine clearance-based dosing). True = renal adjustment logic embedded; False = no renal adjustment required. Supports clinical decision support (CDS) alerts in CPOE.
attributes.references: Epic Willow; Cerner PharmNet; FDA Drug Labeling; AHRQ Medication Safety

attributes.name: set_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the order set's clinical purpose, intended patient population, and scope of included orders. Supports clinical documentation improvement (CDI) and provider education.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: set_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the pre-defined, evidence-based order set bundle as displayed in the Computerized Physician Order Entry (CPOE) interface (e.g., 'Sepsis Bundle — Adult ICU', 'Community-Acquired Pneumonia Admission Orders').
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; CPOE Standards

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which the order set was sourced. 'epic' = Epic Orders/CPOE; 'cerner' = Cerner Millennium PowerChart; 'meditech' = MEDITECH Expanse; 'manual' = manually entered outside a standard EHR system.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; MEDITECH Expanse; HL7 FHIR

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Native identifier of the order set in the originating operational system (e.g., Epic Orders internal record ID, Cerner Millennium order set catalog ID). Supports ETL lineage tracking and cross-system reconciliation.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HL7 FHIR

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the order set record in the source system or lakehouse. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements, and ETL incremental load processing.
attributes.references: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164); Joint Commission (TJC); HIM Governance; ISO 27001

attributes.name: usage_count
attributes.description: Cumulative count of the number of times this order set version has been activated by providers in CPOE. Supports utilization analytics, adoption tracking, and clinical quality improvement initiatives. Not a calculated aggregate — sourced directly from the EHR order set activation log.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HEDIS; NCQA Quality Reporting

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Semantic version number of the order set (e.g., '1.0', '2.3', '3.1.2'). Incremented upon each approved revision to support version control, audit trails, and rollback capabilities per Health Information Management (HIM) governance requirements.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HIM Governance

attributes.name: weight_based_dosing
attributes.description: Indicates whether any pharmacy orders within the order set use weight-based dosing calculations (e.g., mg/kg). True = weight-based dosing required; False = fixed dosing. Critical for pediatric and oncology order sets and for pharmacy safety validation in Willow/PharmNet.
attributes.references: Epic Willow; Cerner PharmNet; DEA; FDA Drug Safety

products.name: set_item
products.description: Individual order line within an order set, defining each component order that is pre-configured for a care pathway. Captures the parent order set, sequence number, order type, default values (dose, frequency, priority, route), mandatory vs. optional flag, conditional inclusion logic (e.g., if lab value exceeds threshold then include order), conditional logic trigger criteria, age/weight/diagnosis-based inclusion rules, clinical rationale, and alternative order options. Enables granular management of order set content and supports clinical decision support (CDS) rule evaluation at the item level. SSOT for the composition and conditional logic of order set bundles.
products.reference: Epic Order Set Component / Cerner Order Set Detail

attributes.name: set_item_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the order set item. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to radiology.protocol. Business justification: Order set items specifying imaging procedures must reference the radiology protocol to pre-define exam parameters (contrast, prep, sequence). Clinical informatics teams use this link to auto-populate

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.loinc_code. Business justification: set_item represents individual orders within order sets; for lab items, LOINC is the standard identifier. set_item.order_code is plain text. Linking to loinc_code supports lab order set standardizatio

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Order set management: supply-type set_item entries (wound care kits, procedure trays) must reference the specific material_master catalog item to enable formulary compliance checks, cost modeling, and

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.ndc_drug. Business justification: set_item medication items (default_dose, default_route, default_frequency exist on set_item) must reference the authoritative NDC drug record for formulary compliance, drug interaction checking within

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_policy. Business justification: Individual order set items may carry distinct policy requirements beyond the parent set (e.g., a chemotherapy item requires a specific consent policy, a controlled substance item requires a DEA compli

attributes.name: set_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent order set that contains this item. Links this item to its containing order set bundle.

attributes.name: snomed_concept_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.snomed_concept. Business justification: set_item.order_description and diagnosis_criteria are plain text. Linking to snomed_concept supports FHIR ValueSet membership for order set items, clinical decision support conditional inclusion logic

attributes.name: standing_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to order.standing_order. Business justification: An order set item (set_item) can represent a standing order component within an evidence-based order set. When order_type = 'standing_order', the set_item should reference the standing_order master re

attributes.name: test_catalog_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.test_catalog. Business justification: Order set build and maintenance: when a set_item represents a lab test, it must reference the test_catalog for specimen requirements, turnaround times, and orderable status. This link is essential for

attributes.name: age_max_years
attributes.description: Maximum patient age in years for which this order item is appropriate. Used for age-based inclusion rules. Null indicates no maximum age restriction.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Item Age Restrictions

attributes.name: age_min_years
attributes.description: Minimum patient age in years for which this order item is appropriate. Used for age-based inclusion rules. Null indicates no minimum age restriction.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Item Age Restrictions

attributes.name: alternative_order_options
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of alternative order codes that can be substituted for this item. Supports clinical flexibility and formulary management.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Item Alternatives

attributes.name: body_site
attributes.description: Anatomical location where the procedure or specimen collection should be performed. Uses standardized anatomical terminology.
attributes.references: SNOMED CT Body Structure, HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.bodySite

attributes.name: clinical_rationale
attributes.description: Evidence-based justification for including this order in the care pathway. May reference clinical guidelines, protocols, or best practices. Supports clinical decision support.

attributes.name: collection_method
attributes.description: Method by which the specimen should be collected for laboratory orders (e.g., venipuncture, clean catch, biopsy). Ensures proper specimen quality.

attributes.name: condition_expression
attributes.description: Formal expression defining the conditional logic criteria (e.g., age > 65, weight < 50kg, diagnosis = ICD-10:E11.9). Uses clinical decision support (CDS) rule syntax.

attributes.name: condition_type
attributes.description: Category of conditional logic applied to this item. Determines which patient data elements are evaluated for inclusion/exclusion decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: age_based|weight_based|diagnosis_based|lab_value|allergy|medication_interaction|none — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: conditional_inclusion_logic
attributes.description: Rule expression defining when this item should be automatically included or excluded from the order set. Evaluated at order set activation time based on patient context.

attributes.name: contrast_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether contrast media should be used for radiology imaging orders. Affects patient preparation and allergy screening requirements.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this order set item record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and compliance reporting.

attributes.name: default_dose
attributes.description: Pre-configured dose amount for medication orders. May include numeric value and unit (e.g., 500 mg, 10 mL). Can be overridden at order entry.

attributes.name: default_duration
attributes.description: Pre-configured duration for time-limited orders (e.g., 7 days, 2 weeks). Primarily used for medication orders with a defined treatment period.

attributes.name: default_frequency
attributes.description: Pre-configured administration or execution frequency for this order (e.g., BID, TID, QD, Q4H). Primarily used for medication and nursing orders.

attributes.name: default_priority
attributes.description: Pre-configured priority level for this order item. Can be overridden by the ordering provider at the time of order entry.

attributes.name: default_quantity
attributes.description: Pre-configured quantity for orders that require a count or volume (e.g., number of units to dispense, volume of fluid to administer).

attributes.name: default_route
attributes.description: Pre-configured administration route for medication orders (e.g., oral, intravenous, intramuscular, subcutaneous). Can be overridden at order entry.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this order set item is no longer available for use. Null indicates the item remains effective indefinitely. Supports order set retirement and updates.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this order set item becomes available for use. Supports versioning and phased rollout of order set changes.

attributes.name: instruction_text
attributes.description: Additional instructions or guidance for the ordering provider or fulfillment team. Displayed during order entry and on order requisitions.

attributes.name: is_default_selected
attributes.description: Indicates whether this item is pre-selected by default when the order set is opened. Providers can deselect optional items.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Item Configuration

attributes.name: is_mandatory
attributes.description: Indicates whether this order item must be included when the order set is activated. True means the item cannot be deselected by the ordering provider.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Item Configuration

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this order set item record was most recently updated. Supports change tracking and version control.

attributes.name: laterality
attributes.description: Specifies which side of the body the order applies to for paired anatomical structures. Critical for surgical and imaging orders.
attributes.references: SNOMED CT Laterality, HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.bodySite

attributes.name: order_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the order item. Displayed to clinicians during order set selection and order entry.

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Category of clinical order represented by this item. Determines which fulfillment system and workflow will process the order.

attributes.name: patient_instruction_text
attributes.description: Instructions intended for the patient regarding this order (e.g., fasting requirements, preparation steps, post-procedure care). May be printed on patient education materials.

attributes.name: requires_authorization
attributes.description: Indicates whether this order item requires prior authorization from the payer before it can be performed. Used for revenue cycle and utilization management.

attributes.name: requires_consent
attributes.description: Indicates whether explicit patient consent is required before this order can be performed. Used for high-risk procedures and research protocols.

attributes.name: sequence_number
attributes.description: Ordinal position of this item within the parent order set. Determines the display and execution order of items in the set.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Configuration

attributes.name: set_item_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this order set item. Only active items are available for use in clinical order entry.

attributes.name: specimen_type
attributes.description: Type of biological specimen required for laboratory orders (e.g., blood, urine, tissue, swab). Used for specimen collection and handling instructions.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier for this order set item configuration. Supports change tracking and audit requirements for clinical content management.

attributes.name: weight_max_kg
attributes.description: Maximum patient weight in kilograms for which this order item is appropriate. Used for weight-based dosing and inclusion rules. Null indicates no maximum weight restriction.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Item Weight Restrictions

attributes.name: weight_min_kg
attributes.description: Minimum patient weight in kilograms for which this order item is appropriate. Used for weight-based dosing and inclusion rules. Null indicates no minimum weight restriction.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Item Weight Restrictions

products.name: routing
products.description: Operational record capturing how a clinical order is routed to its fulfilling department, lab, pharmacy, or imaging unit. Captures routing rule applied, destination department or facility, routing datetime, routing method (automatic, manual override), routing priority, queue assignment, routing status (queued, acknowledged, rerouted, failed), and queue position. Supports operational visibility into order fulfillment bottlenecks, SLA compliance for STAT and urgent orders, and department workload balancing.
products.reference: Epic Orders Routing / HL7 ORC Routing Segment

attributes.name: routing_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the order routing record. Primary key.

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the facility or campus where the destination department is located. Supports multi-site health systems.

attributes.name: clinical_order_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the clinical order being routed. Links to the parent order from CPOE (Computerized Physician Order Entry) system.

attributes.name: destination_unit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to facility.unit. Business justification: Order routing directs work to specific clinical units (lab, pharmacy, radiology). Linking routing to facility.unit enables unit-level queue management, workload balancing, and turnaround time SLA repo

attributes.name: policy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_policy. Business justification: Order routing decisions must comply with policies governing controlled substance routing, STAT order escalation, and cross-facility routing. Compliance auditors reviewing routing rule adherence need r

attributes.name: acknowledgement_datetime
attributes.description: Timestamp when the receiving department or system acknowledged receipt of the routed order. Used to measure queue wait time.

attributes.name: auto_route_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order was eligible for automatic routing based on order type, priority, and system configuration. False if manual routing was required.

attributes.name: completion_datetime
attributes.description: Timestamp when the routing event was marked complete, indicating the order reached its fulfillment destination and processing began.

attributes.name: created_datetime
attributes.description: Timestamp when the order routing record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: datetime
attributes.description: Timestamp when the order was routed to the destination department or facility. Critical for SLA (Service Level Agreement) tracking and turnaround time analysis.

attributes.name: delay_minutes
attributes.description: Number of minutes the routing event exceeded the SLA target. Null if SLA was met. Used for bottleneck analysis and process improvement.

attributes.name: destination_workstation_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific workstation, instrument, or device to which the order was routed within the destination department. Used for lab analyzers, imaging modalities, and pharmacy dispensing systems.

attributes.name: estimated_completion_datetime
attributes.description: Predicted timestamp when the order fulfillment will be completed, based on current queue depth, workload, and historical turnaround times.

attributes.name: notes

products.name: fulfillment
products.description: Transactional record capturing the completion or execution of a clinical order by the fulfilling department, serving as the order domain's acknowledgment that downstream work was performed. Captures fulfillment datetime, fulfilling provider or technician, fulfillment location, fulfillment method, actual vs. ordered quantity, partial fulfillment indicator, fulfillment notes, exception reason if the order was not fulfilled as ordered, fulfillment status, and turnaround time (order-to-fulfillment elapsed time). Bridges the order intent (clinical_order) with the result or dispensing event in downstream domains (laboratory, radiology, pharmacy). SSOT boundary: this product tracks fulfillment status and timing from the order perspective only. Detailed result data (lab values, imaging reports, dispensing records) is owned by the respective downstream domain — laboratory, radiology, or pharmacy.

attributes.name: pediatric_approved_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the drug has FDA approval for use in pediatric populations with established dosing and safety data.

attributes.name: pregnancy_category

attributes.name: refrigeration_required_flag

attributes.name: renal_dosing_adjustment_flag

attributes.name: route_of_administration

attributes.name: rxnorm_code

attributes.name: storage_temperature_range

attributes.name: strength

attributes.name: therapeutic_category
attributes.description: The clinical therapeutic category indicating the primary disease state or condition the drug is used to treat (e.g., Cardiovascular, Antibiotic, Analgesic, Antidiabetic).

attributes.name: unit_of_measure

products.name: formulary
products.description: Defines the approved drug formulary for each health plan, payer, or facility tier. Captures formulary tier (preferred/non-preferred/specialty), prior authorization requirements, step therapy requirements, quantity limits, formulary effective and expiration dates, therapeutic alternatives, payer-specific coverage rules, and specialty drug classification. Supports formulary management, clinical decision support at point of prescribing, and prescription adjudication. Benefit plan financial details (copay/coinsurance schedules, deductible applicability, mail-order benefit rules) are sourced from the billing domain; this product owns drug-level coverage and access rules only. Sourced from Epic Willow and Cerner PharmNet formulary modules.

products.name: specimen
products.description: Master record for every biological specimen collected for laboratory testing and the SSOT for specimen identity, accessioning, chain of custody, and full specimen lifecycle. Tracks specimen type (blood, urine, tissue, CSF, swab), collection method, collection date/time, collector identity and role, collection site (body location), container type, volume, accession number (LIS-assigned unique work-unit identifier), accession date/time, accession status (received, processing, resulted, archived), receiving lab location, priority, chain-of-custody status, storage location, specimen condition at receipt, number of aliquots, and disposal/retention status. Supports CLIA-compliant specimen tracking from collection through accessioning, testing, and disposal.

products.name: test_result
products.description: Transactional record of every individual laboratory test result produced for a specimen, including result amendments and critical value notifications. Stores LOINC-coded test identifier, result value (numeric, text, coded), result unit of measure, reference range applied, result status lifecycle (preliminary, final, corrected, cancelled), abnormal flag (normal, low, high, critical low, critical high), result date/time, performing lab section, instrument identifier, verifying technologist. Owns the full amendment/correction history: original value, amended value, amendment reason, amending user, amendment timestamp. When a result exceeds critical thresholds, owns the critical value alert lifecycle: alert generation timestamp, notified provider, notification method (phone, secure message, EHR alert), acknowledgment timestamp, acknowledging clinician, escalation actions, and resolution notes. Consolidates the former critical_value_alert and result_amendment concepts. Supports CLIA critical value compliance, Joint Commission NPSG requirements, HIM audit requirements, and downstream clinical decision-making.

products.name: reference_range

Includes lower and upper normal limits, critical low and critical high thresholds, panic value definitions, unit of measure, effective date range, and the authoritative source (CAP, CLIA, manufacturer insert, institutional medical director override). Used by result interpretation logic to assign abnormal flags and trigger critical value alerts in test_result. Supports CLIA-required documentation of reference range sources and periodic review.

attributes.references: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) 42 CFR 493.1253, College of American Pathologists (CAP) Accreditation Requirements

attributes.name: methodology

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next periodic review of this reference range. Supports compliance with CLIA and CAP requirements for annual review and documentation.
attributes.references: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) 42 CFR 493.1253, College of American Pathologists (CAP) Accreditation Requirements

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or special instructions related to this reference range. May include information about interfering substances, pre-analytical requirements, or special patient populations.

attributes.references: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) 42 CFR 493.1253, College of American Pathologists (CAP) Accreditation Requirements

attributes.name: population_basis

attributes.name: pregnancy_status

attributes.name: race_ethnicity

attributes.references: CDC Race and Ethnicity Code Set, National Institutes of Health (NIH) Guidelines

attributes.name: review_status
attributes.description: Current review and approval status of this reference range. Tracks lifecycle state for quality management and compliance purposes.
attributes.references: College of American Pathologists (CAP) Accreditation Requirements

attributes.name: sample_size
attributes.description: Number of individuals in the reference population used to establish this range. CLSI recommends minimum 120 samples for robust reference intervals. Documents statistical validity of the range.

attributes.name: sex
attributes.description: Biological sex for which this reference range applies. Many laboratory tests have sex-specific reference ranges (e.g., hemoglobin, creatinine).

attributes.name: source_citation
attributes.description: Detailed citation or reference to the authoritative source document (e.g., CAP guideline version, manufacturer package insert identifier, peer-reviewed journal article, institutional policy document). Required for CLIA compliance and periodic review.

attributes.name: source_type
attributes.description: The type of authoritative source from which this reference range was derived. CLIA requires documentation of reference range sources.

attributes.name: statistical_method
attributes.description: Statistical method used to calculate the reference interval (e.g., parametric 95% confidence interval, non-parametric percentile method, robust method). Documents the analytical approach per CLSI standards.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The standardized unit of measure for the reference range values (e.g., mg/dL, mmol/L, g/dL, cells/mcL, IU/L). Must match the unit used in test results for proper interpretation.
attributes.references: Unified Code for Units of Measure (UCUM)

attributes.name: upper_normal_limit
attributes.description: The upper boundary of the normal reference range. Values above this threshold are typically flagged as high or abnormal.

products.name: susceptibility_result
products.description: Transactional record of individual antimicrobial susceptibility test results within a microbiology culture workup. Captures the antibiotic agent (NDC or SNOMED coded), minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) value, disk diffusion zone diameter, interpretation (susceptible, intermediate, resistant, susceptible-dose dependent), testing method (Kirby-Bauer, broth microdilution, E-test), and CLSI breakpoint version applied. Supports antibiotic stewardship and infection control programs.

attributes.description: Human-readable name of the antimicrobial agent tested (e.g., Penicillin, Vancomycin, Ciprofloxacin).

attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) Breakpoint Version
attributes.description: Version of the CLSI M100 Performance Standards document used to interpret the susceptibility result. Breakpoints are updated annually and version is critical for accurate interpretation (e.g., M100-Ed31, M100-Ed32).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this susceptibility result record was first created in the data platform. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.description: Zone of inhibition diameter measured in millimeters for disk diffusion (Kirby-Bauer) susceptibility testing method. Larger zones indicate greater susceptibility.
attributes.references: CLSI M02 Disk Diffusion Performance Standards

attributes.name: inducible_resistance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether inducible resistance was detected (e.g., inducible clindamycin resistance in Staphylococcus, inducible AmpC in Enterobacteriaceae). True indicates inducible resistance detected; False indicates not detected.

attributes.name: infection_control_alert_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this result triggered an infection control alert due to detection of multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO), reportable organism, or outbreak-associated pathogen. True indicates alert generated.

attributes.name: mic_operator
attributes.description: Comparison operator for the MIC value when the exact value is at or beyond the test range limits (e.g., <=0.5 indicates at or below the lowest tested concentration).

attributes.name: mic_unit
attributes.business_glossary_term: Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) Unit of Measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the MIC value, typically micrograms per milliliter (mcg/mL) or milligrams per liter (mg/L).

attributes.name: mic_value
attributes.description: Minimum inhibitory concentration value representing the lowest concentration of antimicrobial agent that inhibits visible growth of the organism. Expressed as a numeric value with unit of measure.

attributes.name: panel_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the standardized panel or battery of antimicrobial agents tested together (e.g., Gram Positive Panel, Gram Negative Panel, Anaerobe Panel). Panels are organism-specific.

attributes.name: panel_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the antimicrobial susceptibility panel tested (e.g., Gram Positive Cocci Panel, Enterobacteriaceae Panel, Pseudomonas Panel).

attributes.name: quality_control_status
attributes.description: Status of quality control testing performed concurrently with patient susceptibility testing. Passed indicates QC organisms yielded expected results; Failed indicates out-of-range QC results requiring investigation.
attributes.references: CLIA Quality Control Requirements, CLSI M100

attributes.name: reportable_to_public_health_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this susceptibility result is reportable to public health authorities (e.g., state health department, CDC) due to detection of notifiable disease or antimicrobial resistance pattern. True indicates reportable.
attributes.references: CDC National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System

attributes.name: resistance_gene
attributes.description: Specific resistance gene detected through molecular testing (e.g., mecA, vanA, blaNDM, blaKPC). Used for epidemiological tracking and infection control.

attributes.name: resistance_mechanism
attributes.description: Known or suspected mechanism of antimicrobial resistance detected (e.g., ESBL, Carbapenemase, MRSA, VRE, AmpC). Critical for infection control and antibiotic stewardship.

attributes.name: resistant_breakpoint
attributes.description: MIC breakpoint value at or above which the organism is classified as resistant according to CLSI guidelines. Used for automated interpretation.

attributes.name: result_comment
attributes.description: Free-text comment or interpretive note from the laboratory regarding the susceptibility result. May include recommendations for therapy, warnings about resistance patterns, or technical notes.

attributes.name: result_status
attributes.description: Current status of the susceptibility result in its lifecycle. Preliminary results may be released before final verification; Final results have been verified and released; Corrected indicates an amendment to a previously final result.

attributes.name: result_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the susceptibility test result was generated or finalized by the laboratory information system. Represents the business event time of result availability.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the source laboratory information system (LIS) that generated this susceptibility result (e.g., Epic Beaker, Cerner PathNet, Sunquest). Used for data lineage and integration troubleshooting.

attributes.name: susceptibility_interpretation
attributes.description: Clinical interpretation of the susceptibility test result based on CLSI breakpoints. Susceptible indicates the organism is inhibited by achievable drug concentrations; Intermediate indicates uncertain efficacy; Resistant indicates the organism is not inhibited by normally achievable concentrations; Susceptible-dose dependent indicates efficacy depends on dosing regimen.

attributes.name: susceptible_breakpoint
attributes.description: MIC breakpoint value at or below which the organism is classified as susceptible according to CLSI guidelines. Used for automated interpretation.

attributes.name: synergy_test_result
attributes.description: Result of synergy testing for combination antimicrobial therapy (e.g., beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor combinations). Positive indicates synergistic effect detected.

attributes.name: testing_method
attributes.description: Laboratory method used to perform the susceptibility test. Common methods include broth microdilution (gold standard for MIC), disk diffusion (Kirby-Bauer), E-test (gradient diffusion), and automated systems (e.g., VITEK, Phoenix).
attributes.value_regex: broth microdilution|disk diffusion|E-test|automated system|agar dilution|gradient diffusion

attributes.description: Date and time when this susceptibility result record was last modified in the data platform. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: verified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the susceptibility result was verified and approved for clinical use by authorized laboratory personnel (medical technologist or pathologist).

SSOT for blood product inventory, traceability, and regulatory compliance. Supports AABB standards, FDA blood establishment regulations, and hemovigilance reporting.

attributes.name: leukoreduction_status

attributes.name: product_type

products.description: Reference master of all laboratory tests and test panels offered by the health system, serving as the SSOT for the laboratory test compendium. For individual tests: captures LOINC code, test name, CPT code(s) for billing, specimen requirements, container type, minimum volume, storage and transport conditions, turnaround time targets (routine and STAT), performing lab (internal section or reference lab name), methodology, and orderable flag. Also covers send-out test catalog entries with reference lab routing information. Consolidates the former test_panel product. Used by clinicians, order entry systems (CPOE), clinical decision support, and CDM charge alignment.

attributes.name: aerobic_requirement
attributes.description: Oxygen requirement for organism growth, critical for culture media selection and incubation conditions in microbiology laboratories.

attributes.name: antibiotic_resistance_profile
attributes.description: Known or typical antibiotic resistance patterns for this organism, including multidrug-resistant (MDR), extensively drug-resistant (XDR), or pan-drug-resistant (PDR) classifications.

attributes.name: biosafety_level
attributes.description: Required biosafety containment level for handling this organism in laboratory settings, ranging from BSL-1 (minimal risk) to BSL-4 (maximum containment).

attributes.name: clinical_significance
attributes.description: Description of the clinical importance and disease associations of this organism, including typical presentations and severity of infections.

attributes.name: common_infection_sites
attributes.description: Typical anatomical sites or body systems where this organism causes infection (e.g., respiratory, urinary tract, bloodstream, skin), used for clinical correlation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this organism reference record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: culture_media_requirements
attributes.description: Specific culture media and growth conditions required for laboratory isolation and identification of this organism (e.g., blood agar, chocolate agar, selective media).

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when this organism reference record became effective and available for use in laboratory information systems.

attributes.name: environmental_reservoir
attributes.description: Natural environmental sources or reservoirs where this organism is commonly found (e.g., soil, water, animals, plants, healthcare environment).

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when this organism reference record is no longer valid for use, typically due to taxonomy reclassification or nomenclature updates.

attributes.name: gram_stain_result
attributes.description: Gram staining classification of bacterial organisms, critical for initial identification and antibiotic selection. Not applicable for non-bacterial organisms.

attributes.name: identification_methods
attributes.description: Laboratory methods and techniques used for definitive identification of this organism (e.g., biochemical tests, mass spectrometry, molecular methods, sequencing).

attributes.name: incubation_duration_hours
attributes.description: Typical incubation time in hours required for visible growth or detection of this organism in laboratory cultures.

attributes.name: incubation_temperature_celsius
attributes.description: Optimal temperature in degrees Celsius for culturing and growing this organism in laboratory settings.

attributes.name: isolation_precautions
attributes.description: Recommended infection control precautions for patients infected with this organism (e.g., standard, contact, droplet, airborne, protective environment).

attributes.name: loinc_code
attributes.description: LOINC code associated with laboratory tests for identifying or detecting this organism, supporting standardized test result reporting.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this organism reference record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: morphology
attributes.description: Microscopic morphological characteristics of the organism (e.g., cocci, bacilli, spiral, yeast, hyphae) used in laboratory identification.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional free-text notes, comments, or special considerations related to this organism for laboratory staff reference.

attributes.name: organism_code
attributes.description: Standardized code representing the organism, typically aligned with SNOMED CT or laboratory information system coding standards.

attributes.name: organism_name
attributes.description: Common or scientific name of the organism as used in clinical and laboratory contexts.

attributes.name: organism_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this organism reference record, indicating whether it is actively used in laboratory systems or has been deprecated due to taxonomy updates.

attributes.name: organism_type
attributes.description: High-level classification of the organism into major biological categories relevant to laboratory diagnostics and infection control.

attributes.name: pathogenicity_level
attributes.description: Classification of the organism's disease-causing potential, used for infection control, biosafety protocols, and clinical interpretation.

attributes.name: reportable_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether detection of this organism requires mandatory reporting to public health authorities at state, national, or international levels.

attributes.name: scientific_name
attributes.description: Full binomial or trinomial scientific name of the organism following taxonomic nomenclature standards (genus, species, subspecies).

attributes.name: specimen_types
attributes.description: Types of clinical specimens from which this organism is typically isolated or detected (e.g., blood, urine, sputum, wound, stool, cerebrospinal fluid).

attributes.name: taxonomy_class
attributes.description: Class-level taxonomic classification of the organism within the biological hierarchy.

attributes.name: taxonomy_family
attributes.description: Family-level taxonomic classification of the organism, grouping related genera together.

attributes.name: taxonomy_genus
attributes.description: Genus-level taxonomic classification, the first part of the binomial scientific name (e.g., Staphylococcus, Escherichia).

attributes.name: taxonomy_kingdom
attributes.description: Highest taxonomic rank classification of the organism (e.g., Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya, Viruses) per biological taxonomy standards.

attributes.name: taxonomy_order
attributes.description: Order-level taxonomic classification of the organism, further refining the biological classification hierarchy.

attributes.name: taxonomy_phylum
attributes.description: Phylum-level taxonomic classification of the organism, providing intermediate hierarchical context for biological classification.

attributes.name: taxonomy_species
attributes.description: Species-level taxonomic classification, the second part of the binomial scientific name (e.g., aureus, coli).

attributes.name: transmission_mode
attributes.description: Primary modes of transmission for this organism (e.g., airborne, droplet, contact, vector-borne, foodborne, waterborne), critical for infection prevention and control.

attributes.name: zoonotic_potential
attributes.description: Indicates whether this organism can be transmitted between animals and humans, important for occupational health and epidemiological tracking.

domains.name: radiology
domains.description: Medical imaging and diagnostic radiology services. Owns imaging orders, modality scheduling (CT, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound, PET), PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System) integration, radiology reports, DICOM image metadata, contrast administration, radiation dose tracking, radiologist interpretations, and CPT-coded procedures. Integrates with RIS (Radiology Information System) including Epic Radiant and Cerner RadNet.

products.name: imaging_order
products.description: Core transactional record of every radiology imaging order placed via CPOE (Epic Radiant / Cerner RadNet). Captures the full lifecycle from placement through completion including status history audit trail. Stores ordering provider NPI, patient MRN, modality type (CT, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound, PET, fluoroscopy), clinical indication, ICD-10 diagnosis codes, CPT procedure codes, order priority (STAT, routine, urgent), order status with full status transition history, requisition number, referring department, and RIS accession number. SSOT for radiology order identity and lifecycle within the RIS workflow. Aligns with HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest and IHE SWF (Scheduled Workflow) profile.

attributes.name: is_external_import

attributes.name: pacs_status

attributes.name: patient_sex

attributes.name: priority

attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameters; CMS Radiology Quality Reporting; Epic Radiant Report Sign-off

attributes.name: report_status

attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameters for Communication; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.status; Epic Radiant Report Status

attributes.name: ris_system_source

attributes.name: series_count

attributes.name: size_mb

attributes.name: start_timestamp

attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 (0008,0030); IHE RAD TF; ACR Radiology Metrics

attributes.name: study_date

attributes.name: study_description

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

Captures Series Instance UID, series number, series description, modality, body part, acquisition date and time, number of images in series, slice thickness, pixel spacing, image orientation, series status, and PACS storage path. Enables granular navigation of imaging data at the series level for radiologist review and PACS retrieval. Aligns with HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy.series component and IHE RAD profiles for image management.

attributes.description: Indicates whether contrast agent was administered during the imaging study. Relevant for CPT code selection, billing accuracy, radiation safety, and clinical documentation of contrast reactions.

attributes.name: contrast_agent_name
attributes.description: Name of the contrast agent administered during the imaging study (e.g., Gadolinium, Iohexol, Gadobutrol). Null if no contrast was administered. Used for adverse event tracking, pharmacy reconciliation, and clinical documentation.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; FDA Drug Labeling; NDC; Epic Willow Pharmacy

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the radiology report record was first created in the source system. Represents the audit creation timestamp for the report entity. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and compliance reporting.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b) — Audit Controls; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF

attributes.name: critical_finding_communicated_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the critical finding has been communicated to the ordering or responsible provider. Required for Joint Commission compliance. Only applicable when critical_finding_flag is True.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission NPSG.02.03.01; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings

attributes.name: critical_finding_communicated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the critical finding was communicated to the ordering or responsible provider. Used to measure turnaround time compliance with Joint Commission and ACR critical results communication standards.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission NPSG.02.03.01; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings

attributes.name: critical_finding_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the report contains a critical or urgent finding that requires immediate communication to the ordering provider per ACR and Joint Commission guidelines. When True, triggers a critical results notification workflow. Supports patient safety and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission NPSG.02.03.01; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: dicom_study_instance_uid
attributes.description: Globally unique DICOM Study Instance UID linking this report to the corresponding image set in the Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS). Enables direct navigation from the report to the source images. Sourced from DICOM tag (0020,000D).
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0020,000D); IHE RAD-28; PACS Integration Standards

attributes.name: dictation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the radiologist began dictating the report. Used to measure report turnaround time (TAT) from study completion to dictation. Sourced from Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet workflow timestamps.
attributes.references: ACR Radiology Reporting Turnaround Time Guidelines; IHE RAD-28; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: findings_text
attributes.description: Full narrative text of the radiologist's findings section of the report, describing the imaging observations in detail. Contains Protected Health Information (PHI). This is the primary clinical content of the report and the source of truth for diagnostic observations. Sourced from Epic ClinDoc or Cerner PowerChart dictation/transcription.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.text; IHE RAD-28; ACR Reporting Guidelines

attributes.name: follow_up_recommendation
attributes.description: Structured follow-up recommendation from the radiologist's impression, indicating the recommended next action (e.g., 'Follow-up CT in 3 months', 'Biopsy recommended', 'No follow-up needed'). Used for care coordination, population health management, and closing the loop on incidental findings.
attributes.references: ACR Reporting Guidelines; The Joint Commission; CMS Quality Reporting; NCQA HEDIS

attributes.name: impression_text
attributes.description: Radiologist's summary impression or conclusion section of the report, providing the diagnostic interpretation and clinical recommendations. Contains Protected Health Information (PHI). This is the most clinically actionable section of the report and is used for clinical decision support, CDI, and quality measurement.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.conclusion; IHE RAD-28; ACR Reporting Guidelines

attributes.name: laterality
attributes.description: Indicates the side of the body examined when applicable (left, right, bilateral, or unspecified). Critical for surgical safety, billing accuracy, and clinical documentation. Sourced from DICOM tag (0020,0060) and RIS.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0020,0060); The Joint Commission National Patient Safety Goals; ICD-10-CM

attributes.name: modality_code
attributes.description: DICOM-standard code identifying the imaging modality used for the study (e.g., CT = Computed Tomography, MR = Magnetic Resonance Imaging, XR/DX/CR = X-Ray, US = Ultrasound, PT = Positron Emission Tomography, NM = Nuclear Medicine, MG = Mammography, FL = Fluoroscopy). Sourced from DICOM tag (0008,0060). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|MR|XR|US|PT|NM|MG|FL|DX|CR — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0008,0060); ACR Practice Parameters; IHE RAD-28

attributes.name: preliminary_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the report was first released in preliminary status, making it available to ordering providers before final attestation. Key lifecycle event for TAT measurement and clinical workflow.
attributes.references: IHE RAD-28; ACR Radiology Reporting Turnaround Time Guidelines; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport

attributes.name: radiation_dose_ctdi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Radiation Dose CT Dose Index Volume (CTDIvol) mGy
attributes.description: CT Dose Index Volume (CTDIvol) in mGy representing the average radiation dose per unit length for CT studies. Null for non-CT modalities. Used alongside DLP for comprehensive radiation dose monitoring and ACR Dose Index Registry reporting.
attributes.references: ACR Dose Index Registry; NCRP Report No. 172; FDA Radiation-Emitting Products; IHE REM Profile; DICOM PS3.3

attributes.name: radiation_dose_dlp
attributes.business_glossary_term: Radiation Dose Dose Length Product (DLP) mGy·cm
attributes.description: Dose Length Product (DLP) in mGy·cm representing the total radiation dose delivered during the CT or fluoroscopy study. Null for non-ionizing modalities (MRI, Ultrasound). Used for radiation dose monitoring, ACR Dose Index Registry reporting, and patient safety compliance.
attributes.references: ACR Dose Index Registry; NCRP Report No. 172; FDA Radiation-Emitting Products; IHE REM Profile; DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0040,A124)

attributes.name: rads_category
attributes.description: Standardized ACR Reporting and Data System (RADS) assessment category assigned in the impression (e.g., BI-RADS 0-6 for mammography, LI-RADS 1-5 for liver, TI-RADS 1-5 for thyroid, Lung-RADS 1-4). Drives follow-up recommendations and quality measurement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BI-RADS 0|BI-RADS 1|BI-RADS 2|BI-RADS 3|BI-RADS 4|BI-RADS 5|BI-RADS 6|LI-RADS 1|LI-RADS 2|LI-RADS 3|LI-RADS 4|LI-RADS 5|TI-RADS 1|TI-RADS 2|TI-RADS 3|TI-RADS 4|TI-RADS 5|Lung-RADS 1|Lung-RADS 2|Lung-RADS 3|Lung-RADS 4 — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ACR BI-RADS Atlas; ACR LI-RADS; ACR Lung-RADS; ACR TI-RADS; NCQA HEDIS

attributes.name: report_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the radiology report. Drives clinical decision-making and downstream notification workflows. 'Preliminary' indicates a draft interpretation; 'final' indicates the signed, attested report; 'addendum' and 'amended' indicate post-final modifications. Aligns with HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.status.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.status; IHE RAD-28; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: ris_report_code
attributes.description: Native report identifier from the source Radiology Information System (RIS), such as Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet. Used for cross-system reconciliation, ETL lineage tracking, and source system audit.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; IHE RAD-28

attributes.name: signing_radiologist_npi
attributes.description: 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the radiologist who signed and attested the final report. Required for CMS billing, claims submission, and provider credentialing validation. Sourced from the NPPES registry.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Final Rule 45 CFR Part 162; HIPAA 45 CFR §162.406; CMS-1500; UB-04

attributes.name: stat_priority_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the imaging order and report were designated as STAT (immediate/urgent priority), requiring expedited turnaround time. Drives workflow prioritization in the RIS and radiologist worklist. Used for TAT compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: ACR Radiology Reporting Turnaround Time Guidelines; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: study_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the imaging study was performed (image acquisition). This is the principal real-world event time for the report. Sourced from DICOM tag (0008,0020)/(0008,0030) and RIS. Used as the primary temporal anchor for TAT calculations and clinical timelines.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tags (0008,0020) and (0008,0030); IHE RAD-28; HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy.started

attributes.name: study_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the imaging study protocol or procedure performed (e.g., 'CT Chest with Contrast', 'MRI Brain without Contrast'). Sourced from the RIS order and DICOM tag (0008,1030). Used for report titling and clinical context.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0008,1030); Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: template_code
attributes.description: Reference to the structured reporting template used to generate the report (e.g., ACR-standardized templates, site-specific templates). Supports structured reporting initiatives, quality measurement, and AI-assisted reporting workflows.
attributes.references: ACR Reporting and Data Systems (RADS); IHE RAD-28; RadReport Template Library

attributes.name: transcription_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the report transcription was completed (if applicable). Relevant for facilities using human transcription services rather than voice recognition. Used in TAT measurement.
attributes.references: IHE RAD-28; ACR Radiology Reporting Turnaround Time Guidelines; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the radiology report record was last modified in the source system. Used for incremental data loading, change data capture (CDC), and audit trail maintenance.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b) — Audit Controls; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF; ETL Best Practices

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Sequential version number of the report, starting at 1 for the initial report and incrementing with each amendment or addendum. Enables tracking of the full amendment history and identification of the current authoritative version.
attributes.references: IHE RAD-28; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport; HIM Documentation Standards
