attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,0015); SNOMED CT; RSNA RadLex Anatomy

attributes.name: clinical_indication
attributes.description: The clinical reason or diagnostic question driving the imaging order for which this protocol is designed (e.g., 'Pulmonary Embolism Rule-Out', 'Abdominal Pain', 'Stroke Workup'). Maps to ICD-10 diagnosis categories and supports appropriateness criteria evaluation.
attributes.references: ICD-10-CM; ACR Appropriateness Criteria; CMS LCD Policies

attributes.name: contrast_dose_ml
attributes.description: Standard contrast agent dose in milliliters specified for this protocol. May be weight-based (documented separately in patient preparation instructions) or fixed volume. Used for pharmacy preparation and contrast utilization tracking.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; Epic Willow Pharmacy; FDA Drug Labeling

attributes.name: contrast_flow_rate_ml_per_sec
attributes.description: Injection flow rate for intravenous contrast in milliliters per second as specified in the protocol. Critical for CT angiography and dynamic phase imaging to achieve optimal vascular enhancement. Null for non-IV contrast protocols.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; RSNA Contrast Administration Guidelines

attributes.name: contrast_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether intravenous or oral contrast administration is required for this protocol. True = contrast is required; False = non-contrast study. Drives pre-procedure screening for contrast allergies, renal function checks, and pharmacy preparation.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; Epic Radiant Protocol Library; FDA Drug Safety Communications

attributes.name: contrast_route
attributes.description: Route of administration for the contrast agent specified in this protocol (e.g., intravenous for CT angiography, oral for GI studies, intrathecal for myelography). Drives nursing preparation and patient consent requirements.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; Epic Willow Pharmacy Integration; Joint Commission Medication Safety

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this protocol record was first created in the radiology data platform. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and compliance with HIPAA record retention requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; Joint Commission Record Retention Standards; ISO 27001

attributes.name: dose_optimization_program
attributes.description: Radiation dose optimization program under which this protocol was designed or benchmarked. 'image_gently' for pediatric dose reduction, 'image_wisely' for adult dose reduction, 'acr_dir' for ACR Dose Index Registry benchmarking. Supports regulatory reporting and quality improvement programs.
attributes.references: Image Gently Campaign; Image Wisely Program; ACR Dose Index Registry; NCRP Report 172

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this protocol version becomes effective and available for clinical use in the RIS. May differ from approval_date if a future activation date is set. Used for version control and ensuring technologists use the current protocol.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Protocol Library; ACR Practice Parameters; Joint Commission Standards

attributes.name: fasting_duration_hours
attributes.description: Required fasting duration in hours prior to the examination when fasting_required is True (e.g., 4 hours for contrast CT, 6 hours for PET-CT). Null when fasting is not required.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; ACR Practice Parameters; ASA Fasting Guidelines

attributes.name: fasting_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the patient must fast (NPO) prior to this imaging examination. True = fasting required; False = no fasting required. Drives pre-procedure patient instructions and scheduling communication.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; ACR Practice Parameters; Joint Commission Patient Safety Goals

attributes.name: field_of_view_mm
attributes.description: Field of view in millimeters defining the anatomical coverage area for image reconstruction. Determines spatial resolution and the extent of anatomy captured in the image matrix. Applicable to CT and MRI protocols.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,1164); ACR Practice Parameters; RSNA Imaging Guidelines

attributes.name: implant_screening_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether MRI implant safety screening is required before performing this protocol. True = screening required (applicable to all MRI protocols); False = not required. Drives pre-procedure safety questionnaire workflows to identify contraindicated implants, pacemakers, or metallic foreign bodies.
attributes.references: ACR MRI Safety Guidelines; FDA MRI Device Guidance; Joint Commission Patient Safety Goals

attributes.name: kvp
attributes.description: Peak kilovoltage (kVp) setting for the X-ray tube as specified in this protocol. Determines X-ray beam energy and affects image contrast and patient radiation dose. Applicable to CT, X-ray, and fluoroscopy modalities. Null for MRI and ultrasound.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,0060); ACR-AAPM Technical Standards; NCRP Report 172

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this protocol record was most recently modified in the radiology data platform. Used for change tracking, audit trails, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver layer.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; Joint Commission Record Retention Standards; ISO 27001

attributes.name: magnetic_field_strength_tesla
attributes.description: Magnetic field strength in Tesla for MRI protocols (e.g., 1.5T, 3.0T, 7.0T). Determines scanner compatibility, image quality characteristics, and specific absorption rate (SAR) limits. Null for non-MRI modalities.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,0087); ACR MRI Safety Guidelines; FDA MRI Device Guidance

attributes.name: mas
attributes.description: Milliampere-seconds (mAs) setting specifying the X-ray tube current-time product for this protocol. Directly influences image noise and patient radiation dose. Used in CT and radiography protocols. Null for MRI and ultrasound.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,1152); ACR-AAPM Technical Standards; NCRP Report 172

attributes.name: modality_type
attributes.description: DICOM-standard imaging modality code for which this protocol is defined (e.g., CT = Computed Tomography, MRI = Magnetic Resonance Imaging, XR = X-Ray, US = Ultrasound, PET = Positron Emission Tomography, NM = Nuclear Medicine, MG = Mammography). Drives scheduling to the correct equipment and technologist skill set. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|MRI|XR|US|PET|NM|MG|FL|DX|PT — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3; ACR Practice Parameters; Epic Radiant Modality Configuration

attributes.name: pacs_routing_code
attributes.description: Code used to route completed images to the correct reading worklist, hanging protocol, and storage location within the Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS). Ensures images are delivered to the appropriate radiologist subspecialty queue for interpretation.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.4 Storage SOP Classes; Epic Radiant PACS Integration; ACR Informatics Standards

attributes.name: patient_population
attributes.description: Target patient population for which this protocol is designed. Drives protocol selection logic in the RIS based on patient age and clinical context. Pediatric and neonatal protocols use weight-based dosing and modified acquisition parameters.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameters; Image Gently Campaign; Image Wisely Program; CMS Pediatric Quality Measures

attributes.name: patient_prep_instructions
attributes.description: Standardized patient preparation instructions for this protocol, including fasting requirements (e.g., NPO 4 hours), hydration instructions, medication holds (e.g., hold Metformin for contrast studies), bowel preparation, and breath-hold coaching. Displayed to scheduling staff and communicated to patients prior to the exam.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; Epic Radiant Patient Instructions; Joint Commission Patient Safety Goals

attributes.name: pitch_factor
attributes.description: Helical pitch factor for CT protocols, defined as table feed per rotation divided by total collimation. Values less than 1.0 indicate overlapping acquisitions (higher dose, better quality); values greater than 1.0 indicate faster coverage with lower dose. Null for non-helical CT and other modalities.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,9311); ACR-AAPM Technical Standards; NCRP Report 172

attributes.name: protocol_category
attributes.description: Clinical category classifying the purpose of this imaging protocol. 'diagnostic' for standard clinical workup, 'screening' for population health programs (e.g., lung cancer screening), 'interventional' for image-guided procedures, 'research' for IRB-approved studies, 'emergency' for ED/trauma protocols, 'pediatric' for age-specific protocols.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameters; CMS Coverage Determinations; IRB Research Protocols

attributes.name: protocol_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the protocol within the Radiology Information System (RIS), such as Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet. Used for order mapping, PACS integration, and cross-system reference.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Protocol Library; Cerner RadNet; ACR Practice Parameters

attributes.name: protocol_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the imaging acquisition protocol as displayed in the RIS and PACS worklist (e.g., 'CT Abdomen Pelvis with Contrast', 'MRI Brain without Contrast'). Used by technologists and radiologists to identify the correct acquisition procedure.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Protocol Library; ACR Practice Parameters; RSNA RadLex

attributes.name: protocol_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the imaging protocol. 'active' indicates the protocol is approved and available for use; 'draft' indicates pending approval; 'retired' indicates superseded by a newer version; 'under_review' indicates undergoing clinical review.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Protocol Library; Joint Commission Standards; ACR Practice Parameters

attributes.name: pulse_sequence_type
attributes.description: MRI pulse sequence type used in this protocol (e.g., 'T1 SE', 'T2 FSE', 'FLAIR', 'DWI', 'GRE', 'SSFP', 'EPI'). Defines the fundamental MRI acquisition technique and determines tissue contrast characteristics. Null for non-MRI modalities.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,9005); ACR MRI Practice Parameters; RSNA RadLex

attributes.name: radiation_dose_ctdi_vol_mgy
attributes.description: Reference CT Dose Index Volume (CTDIvol) in milligray representing the average radiation dose within the scan volume for this CT protocol. Standardized metric for comparing dose across CT scanners and protocols. Reported to ACR Dose Index Registry and used for DRL benchmarking.
attributes.references: NCRP Report 172; ACR Dose Index Registry; DICOM RDSR Tag (0018,9345); IEC 60601-2-44

attributes.name: radiation_dose_dlp_mgy_cm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reference Radiation Dose - Dose Length Product (DLP) (mGy·cm)
attributes.description: Reference Dose Length Product (DLP) in milligray-centimeters representing the expected radiation dose for this CT protocol under standard conditions. Used for radiation dose optimization programs, comparison against Diagnostic Reference Levels (DRLs), and regulatory reporting to CMS and ACR Dose Index Registry.
attributes.references: NCRP Report 172; ACR Dose Index Registry; CMS Radiation Dose Reporting; IAEA Safety Reports Series No. 87; DICOM RDSR

attributes.name: radlex_code
attributes.description: RSNA RadLex ontology code for the imaging procedure or anatomy associated with this protocol (e.g., RID10321 for CT of abdomen). Supports standardized terminology in radiology reporting, PACS integration, and research data aggregation.
attributes.references: RSNA RadLex Ontology; ACR Informatics Standards; HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy

attributes.name: reconstruction_algorithm
attributes.description: Image reconstruction algorithm specified for this protocol (e.g., 'Filtered Back Projection', 'Iterative Reconstruction', 'Deep Learning Reconstruction', 'ASIR-V 40%'). Affects image quality, noise characteristics, and radiation dose efficiency. Vendor-specific algorithm names are stored as-is.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,1210); ACR-AAPM Technical Standards; RSNA Imaging Informatics

attributes.name: renal_function_check_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether pre-procedure renal function assessment (eGFR/creatinine) is required before administering contrast for this protocol. True = renal check required (standard for iodinated and gadolinium contrast protocols); False = not required. Drives lab order triggers in Epic Radiant.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; CMS Contrast Nephropathy Guidelines; Epic Radiant Pre-Procedure Checks

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date on which this protocol version was retired or superseded by a newer version. Null for currently active protocols. Used for version lifecycle management and historical audit trails.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Protocol Library; ACR Practice Parameters; Joint Commission Standards

attributes.name: ris_procedure_code
attributes.description: Internal procedure code assigned to this protocol within the Radiology Information System (RIS), such as Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet. Used for order entry mapping, scheduling, and charge capture integration with the CDM.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Procedure Dictionary; Cerner RadNet; CMS Charge Description Master (CDM)

attributes.name: scan_duration_estimate_sec
attributes.description: Estimated acquisition time in seconds for this protocol under standard conditions. Used for scheduling slot allocation in the RIS, patient throughput planning, and breath-hold instruction timing for chest and abdominal studies.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Scheduling Configuration; ACR Practice Parameters

attributes.name: sedation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether procedural sedation or anesthesia is required or commonly needed for this protocol (e.g., pediatric MRI, claustrophobic patients). True = sedation required; False = no sedation required. Triggers anesthesia scheduling and pre-sedation assessment workflows.
attributes.references: Joint Commission Sedation Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation; ACR Practice Parameters

attributes.name: slice_thickness_mm
attributes.description: Nominal slice thickness in millimeters for cross-sectional imaging protocols (CT, MRI). Thinner slices provide higher spatial resolution for small structure evaluation; thicker slices reduce noise and radiation dose. Null for planar modalities.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0050,0018); ACR Practice Parameters; RSNA Imaging Guidelines

attributes.name: total_exam_duration_min
attributes.description: Total estimated examination time in minutes including patient preparation, positioning, scanning, and post-processing. Used for scheduling block allocation in the RIS and patient appointment communication. Distinct from scan_duration_estimate_sec which covers acquisition only.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Scheduling; ACR Practice Parameters; CMS Facility Scheduling Guidelines

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Version number of the protocol definition following semantic versioning (e.g., '1.0', '2.3', '3.1.2'). Enables tracking of protocol revisions over time and ensures technologists are using the current approved version.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Protocol Library; ACR Practice Parameters; Joint Commission Standards

products.name: contrast_admin
products.description: Transactional record of contrast agent administration events associated with an imaging study. Captures contrast agent name, NDC (National Drug Code), route of administration (IV, oral, intrathecal), dose administered (mL and mg), injection rate, injection site, pre-medication given flag, pre-medication details, adverse reaction flag, adverse reaction description, eGFR value at time of administration, contrast allergy screening result, administering clinician NPI, and administration datetime. Supports patient safety monitoring, contrast reaction tracking, and pharmacy reconciliation. Aligns with ACR Manual on Contrast Media guidelines and HL7 FHIR MedicationAdministration resource.
products.reference: Contrast Administration Record / ACR Contrast Manual / Epic Willow MAR

This enables usage variance reporting, waste reductio

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.allergy. Business justification: ACR guidelines and patient safety protocols require documenting which specific allergy record was reviewed during contrast screening. Linking contrast_admin to the screened clinical allergy record sup

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the imaging study (DICOM study) with which this contrast administration is associated. Supports PACS integration and study-level traceability.

attributes.name: test_result_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.test_result. Business justification: Contrast administration protocols mandate recent eGFR/creatinine results to assess contrast-induced nephropathy risk. ACR guidelines require documented renal function within specific timeframes. Direc

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical encounter (visit) during which the contrast was administered. Supports revenue cycle and clinical documentation linkage.

attributes.name: accession_number
attributes.description: The Radiology Information System (RIS) accession number assigned to the imaging order. Serves as the primary business identifier linking the contrast event to the RIS workflow in Epic Radiant and Cerner RadNet.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0008,0050); IHE Radiology Technical Framework

attributes.name: administering_clinician_npi
attributes.description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the clinician who administered the contrast agent. Required for regulatory reporting, billing, and provider accountability tracking.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Final Rule 45 CFR Part 162; HIPAA Administrative Simplification; NUCC Health Care Provider Taxonomy

attributes.name: administration_datetime
attributes.description: The precise date and time at which the contrast agent was administered to the patient. This is the principal real-world event timestamp for this transaction, distinct from record audit timestamps.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR MedicationAdministration.effective[x] R4; ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023

attributes.name: administration_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the contrast administration event, aligned with HL7 FHIR MedicationAdministration status codes. 'not-done' indicates contrast was withheld after screening.

attributes.name: adverse_reaction_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time at which the adverse reaction was first observed following contrast administration. Used to calculate time-to-reaction interval for safety analytics.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; FDA MedWatch Reporting Timeline

attributes.name: adverse_reaction_description
attributes.description: Detailed clinical description of the adverse reaction signs and symptoms observed following contrast administration (e.g., 'urticaria on trunk and arms, resolved with diphenhydramine'). Required for FDA MedWatch and internal safety reporting.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; FDA MedWatch 3500A; Joint Commission Sentinel Event Reporting

attributes.name: adverse_reaction_occurred
attributes.description: Indicates whether the patient experienced an adverse reaction following contrast administration (True = reaction occurred, False = no reaction). Triggers mandatory documentation and reporting workflows.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; FDA MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting; Joint Commission Sentinel Event Policy

attributes.name: adverse_reaction_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the adverse reaction experienced by the patient following contrast administration, per ACR grading criteria. Drives escalation protocols and mandatory reporting thresholds.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023 — Adverse Reaction Classification; FDA MedWatch; AHRQ Patient Safety Reporting

attributes.name: adverse_reaction_treatment
attributes.description: Description of the clinical interventions performed to treat the adverse contrast reaction (e.g., 'epinephrine 0.3mg IM, oxygen 4L/min via nasal cannula, IV fluid bolus'). Supports quality review and safety reporting.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; Joint Commission Sentinel Event Policy; AHRQ Patient Safety

attributes.name: agent_class
attributes.description: Classification of the contrast agent by chemical class. Drives safety screening protocols (e.g., gadolinium retention monitoring, iodine allergy screening) and ACR guideline compliance.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; FDA Drug Classification

attributes.name: agent_osmolality_type
attributes.description: Osmolality classification of the iodinated contrast agent (low, iso, or high osmolality). Relevant for patient safety risk stratification, particularly in patients with renal impairment.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023 — Chapter on Iodinated Contrast Media

attributes.name: body_region
attributes.description: The anatomical body region being imaged (e.g., abdomen/pelvis, brain, chest, spine). Used for contrast protocol selection and population health analytics.
attributes.references: SNOMED CT Body Structure Codes; DICOM PS3.3 Body Part Examined Tag (0018,0015)

attributes.name: catheter_gauge
attributes.description: The gauge size of the intravenous catheter used for contrast injection (e.g., 18G, 20G, 22G). Relevant for power injector safety limits and extravasation risk assessment.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; Power Injector Manufacturer Guidelines

attributes.name: concentration_mg_per_ml
attributes.description: The concentration of the contrast agent in the administered preparation, expressed in milligrams per milliliter (mg/mL). Used to verify dose calculations and product selection.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; FDA Drug Labeling Standards

attributes.name: contrast_allergy_screening_result
attributes.description: The result of the pre-administration contrast allergy screening assessment. Captures whether the patient has a documented prior contrast reaction, confirmed allergy, or no known allergy. Drives pre-medication decision.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023 — Allergic-Like Reactions; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

attributes.name: dose_amount_mg
attributes.description: The total mass of contrast agent administered, measured in milligrams (mg). Supports weight-based dosing verification and cumulative gadolinium/iodine exposure tracking.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; FDA Drug Labeling; HL7 FHIR MedicationAdministration.dosage.dose R4

attributes.name: dose_volume_ml
attributes.description: The total volume of contrast agent administered, measured in milliliters (mL). Used for dose tracking, pharmacy reconciliation, and radiation/contrast safety monitoring.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; HL7 FHIR MedicationAdministration.dosage.dose R4

attributes.name: extravasation_occurred
attributes.description: Indicates whether contrast agent extravasation (leakage into surrounding tissue) occurred during injection (True = extravasation, False = no extravasation). Triggers wound care and incident reporting protocols.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023 — Extravasation; Joint Commission Incident Reporting

attributes.name: extravasation_volume_ml
attributes.description: Estimated volume of contrast agent that extravasated into surrounding tissue, in milliliters (mL). Used to guide clinical management and severity classification of the extravasation event.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; Joint Commission Incident Reporting Standards

attributes.name: informed_consent_obtained
attributes.description: Indicates whether informed consent was obtained from the patient prior to contrast administration (True = consent obtained, False = consent not obtained or waived). Required for regulatory compliance and risk management.
attributes.references: Joint Commission Informed Consent Standards RC.02.01.01; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.13; HIPAA

attributes.name: injection_rate_ml_per_sec
attributes.description: The rate at which the contrast agent was injected, expressed in milliliters per second (mL/sec). Relevant for CT bolus timing, power injector programming, and adverse event analysis.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; SNOMED CT; Epic Radiant Power Injector Integration

attributes.name: injection_site
attributes.description: The anatomical site of contrast injection (e.g., right antecubital vein, left hand dorsal vein, lumbar intrathecal space). Supports extravasation tracking and adverse event documentation.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; SNOMED CT Body Site Codes

attributes.name: metformin_held
attributes.description: Indicates whether metformin was held prior to or following contrast administration per ACR guidelines for patients with renal impairment (True = metformin held, False = not held or not applicable).
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023 — Metformin and Iodinated Contrast; FDA Drug Safety Communication

attributes.name: modality
attributes.description: The imaging modality for which the contrast was administered (e.g., CT, MRI, Ultrasound, PET). Determines applicable ACR contrast guidelines and safety protocols. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|MRI|XR|US|PET|NM|FLUORO|ANGIO — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Modality Tag (0008,0060); ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; IHE Radiology Technical Framework

attributes.name: patient_weight_kg
attributes.description: The patient's body weight in kilograms (kg) recorded at the time of contrast administration. Used for weight-based dose calculation verification and contrast safety risk stratification.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; LOINC Code 29463-7

attributes.name: power_injector_used
attributes.description: Indicates whether a power injector device was used to administer the contrast agent (True) or manual hand injection was performed (False). Relevant for injection rate documentation and device safety tracking.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; FDA Medical Device Reporting

attributes.name: pregnancy_status
attributes.description: The patient's pregnancy status at the time of contrast administration screening. Required for contrast safety risk assessment and informed consent documentation per ACR guidelines.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023 — Contrast in Pregnancy; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

attributes.name: premedication_details
attributes.description: Free-text or structured description of the pre-medication regimen administered (e.g., 'Prednisone 50mg PO x3 doses + Diphenhydramine 50mg IV'). Supports clinical documentation and pharmacy reconciliation.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; HL7 FHIR MedicationAdministration Resource R4

attributes.name: premedication_given
attributes.description: Indicates whether pre-medication (e.g., corticosteroid prophylaxis) was administered prior to contrast injection to reduce the risk of allergic reaction (True = pre-medicated, False = not pre-medicated).
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023 — Premedication Protocols; Joint Commission Medication Safety Standards

attributes.name: prior_contrast_reaction_type
attributes.description: Description of the type of prior contrast reaction documented in the patient's allergy history (e.g., urticaria, bronchospasm, anaphylaxis). Informs pre-medication protocol selection.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; SNOMED CT Allergy Reaction Codes

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this contrast administration record was first created in the source system or ingested into the lakehouse Silver layer. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b) — Audit Controls; ISO 27001 A.12.4; HITRUST CSF Control 09.aa

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this contrast administration record was last modified in the source system or updated in the lakehouse Silver layer. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b) — Audit Controls; ISO 27001 A.12.4; HITRUST CSF Control 09.aa

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: The anatomical route by which the contrast agent was delivered to the patient (e.g., intravenous, oral, intrathecal). Critical for adverse reaction risk assessment and clinical documentation.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR MedicationAdministration.dosage.route R4; ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023; NCI Thesaurus Route of Administration

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The originating operational system from which this contrast administration record was sourced (e.g., Epic Radiant, Cerner RadNet). Supports data lineage, ETL audit, and multi-system reconciliation.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR Provenance Resource R4; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

attributes.name: source_system_record_code
attributes.description: The native record identifier from the originating operational system (e.g., Epic Radiant administration event ID, Cerner RadNet medication administration ID). Supports ETL traceability and cross-system reconciliation.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR Provenance Resource R4; HITRUST CSF; IHE PIX/PDQ Integration Profile

attributes.name: thyroid_disease_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the patient has a documented thyroid condition (e.g., hyperthyroidism, thyroid cancer) that may be relevant to iodinated contrast administration safety screening.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023 — Thyroid Considerations; SNOMED CT

products.name: dose_record
products.description: Captures radiation dose metrics for each imaging study involving ionizing radiation (CT, fluoroscopy, nuclear medicine, X-ray). Stores CTDIvol, DLP (Dose Length Product), effective dose estimate (mSv), DAP for fluoroscopy, fluoroscopy time, number of exposures, dose reference level comparison, dose alert flags, RDSR (Radiation Dose Structured Report) UID per IEC 61910 standard, and cumulative patient dose tracking. SSOT for radiation exposure documentation. Supports ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR) reporting, Joint Commission radiation safety requirements, CMS quality programs, and ALARA principle compliance.
products.reference: RDSR / ACR Dose Index Registry / IHE REM Profile

attributes.name: accession_number
attributes.description: Radiology Information System (RIS) accession number uniquely identifying the imaging order/study to which this dose record belongs. Primary business identifier linking dose data to the imaging study in Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3, HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy, ACR DIR

attributes.name: body_part_examined
attributes.description: DICOM-coded body part or anatomical region examined during the imaging study (e.g., CHEST, ABDOMEN, HEAD, PELVIS). Used for dose benchmarking by anatomy and ACR DIR stratification.

attributes.name: contrast_administered
attributes.description: Indicates whether iodinated or gadolinium-based contrast agent was administered during the imaging study. True = contrast used; False = non-contrast study. Relevant for dose context, adverse event tracking, and clinical protocol classification.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media, Epic Radiant, Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: contrast_agent_type
attributes.description: Type of contrast agent administered during the imaging study. 'iodinated'=CT/X-ray contrast; 'gadolinium'=MRI contrast (tracked for nephrogenic systemic fibrosis risk); 'barium'=GI fluoroscopy; 'none'=no contrast. Used for clinical safety monitoring and protocol classification.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media, FDA, Epic Radiant

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this dose record was first created in the source system or ingested into the lakehouse Silver layer. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and regulatory record retention requirements.

attributes.name: ctdivol_mgy
attributes.business_glossary_term: CT Dose Index Volume (CTDIvol) in Milligray (mGy)
attributes.description: Volume CT Dose Index (CTDIvol) in milligray (mGy) for CT studies. Represents the average radiation dose delivered within the scan volume for a single series or the entire study. Primary CT dose metric for ACR DIR benchmarking and dose alert thresholds per NCRP and FDA guidance.
attributes.references: IEC 60601-2-44, ACR DIR, FDA Dose Check, NCRP Report 172

attributes.name: cumulative_dose_msv
attributes.description: Running cumulative effective dose in millisieverts (mSv) for this patient across all prior ionizing radiation imaging studies recorded in the system, including the current study. Supports ALARA principle compliance, radiation safety counseling, and identification of high-dose patients for clinical review.
attributes.references: ALARA Principle, NCRP Report 160, Joint Commission, ACR DIR

attributes.name: dap_gy_cm2
attributes.business_glossary_term: Dose Area Product (DAP) in Gray-Centimeter Squared (Gy·cm²)
attributes.description: Dose Area Product (DAP) in Gy·cm² for fluoroscopy, X-ray angiography, and interventional radiology procedures. Measures total radiation energy delivered to the patient. Primary dose metric for fluoroscopic procedures per IEC 60601-2-43.
attributes.references: IEC 60601-2-43, ACR DIR, NCRP Report 168, Joint Commission

attributes.name: dlp_mgy_cm
attributes.description: Dose Length Product (DLP) in mGy·cm for CT studies. Represents the total radiation energy imparted along the scan length. Used with conversion coefficients to estimate effective dose and is the primary metric for ACR DIR CT dose reporting.
attributes.references: IEC 60601-2-44, ACR DIR, NCRP Report 172, ICRP Publication 102

attributes.name: dose_alert_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this study triggered a radiation dose alert based on institutional or regulatory thresholds (e.g., CTDIvol > alert level, fluoroscopy time > 30 min, RAK > 3 Gy). True = alert triggered; False = within normal limits. Supports Joint Commission radiation safety event reporting.
attributes.references: Joint Commission Sentinel Event Alert, FDA Dose Check (NEMA XR-25), ACR DIR

attributes.name: dose_alert_threshold_type
attributes.description: The specific dose metric that triggered the dose alert, if applicable. Identifies which threshold was exceeded to support targeted clinical review and root cause analysis. 'not_triggered' when dose_alert_flag is False. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ctdivol|dlp|dap|fluoroscopy_time|rak|effective_dose|not_triggered — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA Dose Check (NEMA XR-25), Joint Commission, ACR DIR

attributes.name: dose_alert_value
attributes.description: The numeric threshold value that was exceeded to trigger the dose alert, expressed in the unit of the triggering metric (mGy, mGy·cm, Gy·cm², seconds, or mSv). Supports audit trail for dose safety events.
attributes.references: FDA Dose Check (NEMA XR-25), Joint Commission Sentinel Event Alert

attributes.name: dose_record_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the radiation dose record. 'preliminary' = dose data received but not yet reviewed; 'final' = reviewed and confirmed; 'amended' = corrected after finalization; 'corrected' = technical correction applied; 'cancelled' = study voided.
attributes.references: IEC 61910, ACR DIR, HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport

attributes.name: dose_registry_submission_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR) Submission Status
attributes.description: Status of submission of this dose record to the ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR). 'pending'=queued for submission; 'submitted'=transmitted to ACR DIR; 'accepted'=confirmed by ACR DIR; 'rejected'=rejected by ACR DIR (requires correction); 'not_required'=procedure not in DIR scope.
attributes.references: ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR), CMS Quality Programs, MIPS

attributes.name: dose_registry_submission_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this dose record was submitted to the ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR) or other regulatory dose registry. Supports audit trail for regulatory compliance and CMS quality program reporting.
attributes.references: ACR DIR, CMS MIPS, Joint Commission

attributes.name: drl_comparison_result
attributes.description: Result of comparing the study dose against the applicable national or institutional Diagnostic Reference Level (DRL). 'below_drl'=dose is below the reference level (optimal); 'at_drl'=dose equals reference level; 'above_drl'=dose exceeds reference level (requires review); 'not_applicable'=no DRL defined for this procedure.
attributes.references: ICRP Publication 135, ACR DIR, NCRP Report 172, CMS Quality Programs

attributes.name: effective_dose_msv
attributes.description: Estimated effective dose in millisieverts (mSv) representing the stochastic risk-weighted whole-body equivalent dose. Derived from DLP × conversion coefficient (k-factor) for CT, or from DAP for fluoroscopy. Used for patient communication, cumulative dose tracking, and ALARA compliance.
attributes.references: ICRP Publication 103, NCRP Report 160, ACR DIR, Joint Commission

attributes.name: entrance_skin_dose_mgy
attributes.description: Entrance skin dose (ESD) in milligray (mGy) for radiographic and fluoroscopic procedures. Represents the absorbed dose at the skin entry point. Critical for radiation injury risk assessment and Joint Commission threshold monitoring.
attributes.references: Joint Commission Sentinel Event Alert, NCRP Report 168, IEC 60601-2-43

attributes.name: fluoroscopy_time_sec
attributes.description: Total fluoroscopy beam-on time in seconds for fluoroscopic and interventional procedures. Regulatory threshold monitoring metric; Joint Commission requires tracking and alerting when fluoroscopy time exceeds defined thresholds (e.g., 30 minutes cumulative).
attributes.references: Joint Commission Sentinel Event Alert, IEC 60601-2-43, FDA 21 CFR 1020.32

attributes.name: kvp
attributes.description: Peak kilovoltage (kVp) applied to the X-ray tube during the study. Represents the energy of the X-ray beam. Used for dose optimization, protocol review, and physics quality assurance.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3, ACR Technical Standards, IEC 60601-2-44

attributes.name: modality_type
attributes.description: DICOM modality code indicating the type of imaging equipment used. CT=Computed Tomography, FL=Fluoroscopy, NM=Nuclear Medicine, DX=Digital Radiography (X-ray), MG=Mammography, XA=X-Ray Angiography, RF=Radiofluoroscopy. Determines applicable dose metrics (CTDIvol/DLP for CT, DAP/fluoroscopy time for fluoroscopy). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|FL|NM|DX|MG|XA|RF|PT|SPECT — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.3.1.1.1, ACR DIR, IEC 61910

attributes.name: number_of_exposures
attributes.description: Total count of individual X-ray exposures (radiographic frames or pulses) delivered during the study. Used for dose optimization analysis and comparison against diagnostic reference levels (DRLs).
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 TID 10011, ACR DIR, NCRP Report 172

attributes.name: patient_age_at_study
attributes.description: Patient age in whole years at the time of the imaging study. Used for pediatric dose benchmarking (pediatric patients require lower dose protocols), age-stratified DRL comparisons, and ACR DIR age-group reporting. Derived at time of study to avoid recalculation.
attributes.references: ACR DIR, NCRP Report 172, ICRP Publication 135, Pediatric Imaging Standards

attributes.name: patient_size_cm
attributes.description: Patient effective diameter or water-equivalent diameter in centimeters, used for Size-Specific Dose Estimate (SSDE) calculation in CT. Derived from scout/localizer images or patient measurements. Required for AAPM TG-204 SSDE methodology.
attributes.references: AAPM Report 204 (SSDE), AAPM Report 220, ACR DIR

attributes.name: patient_weight_kg
attributes.description: Patient body weight in kilograms at the time of the imaging study. Used for size-specific dose estimate (SSDE) calculations for CT, weight-based protocol selection, and dose normalization for benchmarking.

attributes.name: physicist_review_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dose record has been flagged for or completed a review by a qualified medical physicist. True = physicist review required or completed; False = no physicist review needed. Triggered by dose alerts, unusual protocol deviations, or regulatory requirements.
attributes.references: Joint Commission Radiation Safety Standards, ACR Practice Parameters, NCRP

attributes.name: physicist_review_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the medical physicist completed the review of this dose record. Null if physicist_review_flag is False or review is pending. Supports compliance audit trail for Joint Commission radiation safety requirements.
attributes.references: Joint Commission Radiation Safety Standards, ACR Practice Parameters

attributes.name: procedure_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the imaging procedure performed (e.g., 'CT Chest with Contrast', 'Fluoroscopic Guidance for Biopsy'). Sourced from the Charge Description Master (CDM) or RIS procedure catalog.
attributes.references: ACR DIR, CDM, Epic Radiant, Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: rdsr_uid
attributes.business_glossary_term: Radiation Dose Structured Report (RDSR) Unique Identifier (UID)
attributes.description: DICOM Radiation Dose Structured Report (RDSR) SOP Instance UID per IEC 61910 standard. Globally unique identifier for the structured dose report generated by the imaging modality. Used for PACS integration and ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR) submission.
attributes.references: IEC 61910, DICOM PS3.3 TID 10011, ACR DIR

attributes.name: reference_air_kerma_mgy
attributes.description: Reference Air Kerma (RAK) in mGy for interventional fluoroscopy procedures. Measured at the interventional reference point (IRP) per IEC 60601-2-43. Used for radiation injury risk assessment and regulatory threshold compliance.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this dose record was sourced (e.g., Epic Radiant, Cerner RadNet, third-party dose management system). Used for data lineage, ETL audit, and multi-system reconciliation in the lakehouse Silver layer.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant, Cerner RadNet, MEDITECH Expanse, IEC 61910

attributes.name: ssde_mgy
attributes.description: Size-Specific Dose Estimate (SSDE) in mGy for CT studies, calculated per AAPM TG-204 methodology by applying a size-based conversion factor to CTDIvol. Provides a more accurate patient-specific dose estimate than CTDIvol alone. Used for pediatric dose optimization and ACR DIR advanced reporting.
attributes.references: AAPM Report 204, AAPM Report 220, ACR DIR

attributes.name: study_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the imaging study was performed. Principal business event date for dose record. Used for trending, regulatory reporting, and cumulative dose period calculations.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3, ACR DIR, Joint Commission

attributes.name: study_instance_uid
attributes.description: DICOM Study Instance UID uniquely identifying the imaging study in the PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System). Enables direct linkage between dose records and DICOM image metadata for audit and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: study_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time the imaging study was performed, including timezone offset. Used for intraday workflow analysis, dose alert timing, and RDSR correlation.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3, IEC 61910, HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy

attributes.name: tube_current_mas
attributes.description: X-ray tube current-time product in milliampere-seconds (mAs) for the study. Directly influences radiation dose output. Used for protocol optimization and dose benchmarking.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3, ACR Technical Standards, IEC 60601-2-44

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this dose record was last modified in the source system or Silver layer. Used for incremental ETL processing, change data capture, and audit trail maintenance.

products.name: critical_result
products.description: Tracks the communication workflow for critical and significant radiology findings requiring immediate clinical action per Joint Commission NPSG.02.03.01. Records finding description, severity level (critical, significant, incidental), notification method (phone, secure message, EHR alert), notified provider NPI, notification datetime, acknowledgment datetime, acknowledgment method, escalation flag, escalation datetime, and Joint Commission compliance status. Supports EMTALA compliance, TJC accreditation requirements, and patient safety event tracking. Aligns with HL7 FHIR CommunicationRequest resource for critical result notification workflows.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.diagnosis. Business justification: TJC NPSG.02.03.01 requires tracking critical radiology findings through to clinical action. Linking a critical result to the resulting clinical diagnosis record documents the care loop closure, suppor

attributes.description: Reference to the provider who placed the original imaging order. May differ from the notified provider if the ordering provider is unavailable. Used for accountability tracking and notification workflow routing.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.requester; CMS CoP §482.26; Epic Radiant Order Management

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient encounter or visit during which the imaging study was performed and the critical finding was identified. Supports EMTALA compliance tracking and care coordination.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR Encounter resource; EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; Epic ADT

attributes.name: accession_number
attributes.description: The RIS-assigned accession number uniquely identifying the imaging order or study that produced the critical finding. Serves as the primary business identifier linking this notification to the originating radiology order in Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 — Attribute Tag (0008,0050); HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy.identifier

attributes.name: acknowledgment_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the notified provider acknowledged receipt and understanding of the critical finding. Required for TJC NPSG.02.03.01 closed-loop communication compliance. Null if acknowledgment has not yet been received.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; HL7 FHIR Communication.received; AHRQ Patient Safety Standards

attributes.name: acknowledgment_method
attributes.description: The communication channel through which the notified provider acknowledged the critical finding. Required for TJC NPSG.02.03.01 closed-loop verification documentation. May differ from the notification method.

attributes.name: acknowledgment_turnaround_minutes
attributes.description: The elapsed time in minutes between notification_datetime and acknowledgment_datetime. Measures provider responsiveness to critical finding notifications. Used for TJC NPSG.02.03.01 compliance measurement and provider performance analytics. Null if acknowledgment has not been received.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; AHRQ Patient Safety Standards; NCQA Quality Measurement

attributes.name: body_part_examined
attributes.description: The anatomical body part or region examined in the imaging study that produced the critical finding. Aligns with DICOM Tag (0018,0015) and SNOMED CT anatomical site codes. Supports clinical analytics and quality reporting.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0018,0015); SNOMED CT Anatomical Structure; HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy.series.bodySite

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this critical finding notification record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and Silver layer ingestion tracking per HIPAA audit control requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b) — Audit Controls; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

attributes.name: dicom_study_uid
attributes.description: The globally unique DICOM Study Instance UID (0020,000D) identifying the imaging study in the PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System). Enables direct linkage to DICOM images for clinical review and audit purposes.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0020,000D) — Study Instance UID; ACR DICOM Standard; HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy.identifier

attributes.name: emtala_applicable
attributes.business_glossary_term: Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) Applicable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether EMTALA obligations apply to this critical finding notification, typically when the patient presented through the Emergency Department. True = EMTALA applies; False = EMTALA not applicable. Supports EMTALA compliance documentation and legal risk management.
attributes.references: EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; CMS EMTALA Enforcement; OIG Compliance Guidance

attributes.name: escalation_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the escalation process was initiated for this critical finding notification. Populated only when escalation_flag is True. Used to measure escalation response times and compliance with institutional escalation policies.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; AHRQ Patient Safety Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.26

attributes.name: escalation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the critical finding notification required escalation due to failure to reach the primary responsible provider within the defined response time threshold. True = escalation was triggered; False = no escalation required. Supports TJC NPSG.02.03.01 compliance and patient safety event tracking.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; AHRQ Patient Safety Event Reporting; OIG Compliance Guidance

attributes.name: escalation_reason
attributes.description: The reason escalation was triggered for this critical finding notification: 'no_response' (provider did not respond within threshold), 'provider_unavailable' (provider not reachable), 'wrong_contact' (incorrect contact information), 'system_failure' (notification system failure), 'other'. Supports root cause analysis and process improvement.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; AHRQ Patient Safety Event Reporting

attributes.name: finding_category
attributes.description: Clinical category of the critical finding (e.g., pulmonary embolism, intracranial hemorrhage, pneumothorax, aortic dissection, malignancy, fracture). Supports population health analytics, quality reporting, and pattern analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pulmonary_embolism|intracranial_hemorrhage|pneumothorax|aortic_dissection|malignancy|fracture|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; SNOMED CT; ICD-10-CM

attributes.name: finding_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the radiologist identified and documented the critical finding during image interpretation. This is the principal business event timestamp representing when the critical result was discovered. Critical for measuring notification turnaround time against TJC NPSG.02.03.01 compliance thresholds.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.effectiveDateTime

attributes.name: finding_description
attributes.description: Free-text clinical description of the critical or significant radiology finding requiring immediate action. Captured from the radiologist's report or preliminary read in the RIS/PACS. Constitutes Protected Health Information (PHI) under HIPAA.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; TJC NPSG.02.03.01; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.conclusion

attributes.name: finding_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the radiology finding: 'critical' (life-threatening, requires immediate action), 'significant' (clinically important, requires timely action), or 'incidental' (unexpected finding not directly related to the primary indication). Drives notification urgency and escalation workflows per TJC NPSG.02.03.01.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; AHRQ Patient Safety Standards

attributes.name: modality
attributes.description: The imaging modality used for the study that produced the critical finding (e.g., CT=Computed Tomography, MRI=Magnetic Resonance Imaging, XR=X-Ray, US=Ultrasound, PET=Positron Emission Tomography, NM=Nuclear Medicine, MG=Mammography, FL=Fluoroscopy). Aligns with DICOM modality codes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|MRI|XR|US|PET|NM|MG|FL — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0008,0060) — Modality; ACR DICOM Standard

attributes.name: mrn
attributes.description: The facility-assigned Medical Record Number (MRN) for the patient associated with the critical finding. Used for cross-system patient identification and audit trail in compliance with HIPAA PHI requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; Epic MPI

attributes.name: notification_attempt_count
attributes.description: The total number of notification attempts made before successful delivery or escalation. Tracks communication persistence and supports root cause analysis for notification failures and escalation triggers.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; AHRQ Patient Safety Standards; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication

attributes.name: notification_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the critical finding notification was transmitted to the responsible provider. Used to calculate notification turnaround time (finding_datetime to notification_datetime) for TJC NPSG.02.03.01 compliance measurement.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; AHRQ Patient Safety Event Reporting; HL7 FHIR CommunicationRequest.occurrenceDateTime

attributes.name: notification_method
attributes.description: The communication channel used to deliver the critical finding notification to the responsible provider (e.g., phone=direct telephone call, secure_message=encrypted messaging platform, ehr_alert=EHR in-basket alert, pager=numeric/alphanumeric pager, in_person=face-to-face, fax=facsimile). Aligns with HL7 FHIR CommunicationRequest.medium.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; HL7 FHIR CommunicationRequest.medium; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312

attributes.name: notification_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of the critical finding notification lifecycle: 'pending' (finding identified, notification not yet sent), 'notified' (notification sent, awaiting acknowledgment), 'acknowledged' (provider confirmed receipt), 'escalated' (escalation triggered due to non-response), 'failed' (notification delivery failed), 'cancelled' (notification voided). Drives workflow management and compliance dashboards.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; HL7 FHIR CommunicationRequest.status; AHRQ Patient Safety Event Tracking

attributes.name: notification_turnaround_minutes

products.name: appointment

attributes.name: care_setting

attributes.name: max_slots_per_session

attributes.name: modified_timestamp

attributes.name: no_show_tracking_enabled_flag

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: overbooking_allowed_flag

attributes.name: overbooking_limit

attributes.name: patient_class

attributes.name: priority_level

attributes.name: recurrence_pattern

attributes.name: recurrence_rule

attributes.name: reminder_enabled_flag

attributes.name: reminder_lead_time_hours
attributes.description: Number of hours before the appointment when the reminder is sent. Null if reminders are not enabled.

attributes.name: service_type_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the type of clinical service provided during appointments scheduled under this template (e.g., 'OFFICE_VISIT', 'SURGERY', 'DIAGNOSTIC').

attributes.name: session_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of the scheduled session in minutes. Calculated as the difference between session start and end times.

attributes.name: session_end_time
attributes.description: Time of day when the scheduled session ends, in HH:MM 24-hour format (e.g., '17:00', '21:00').

attributes.name: session_start_time
attributes.description: Time of day when the scheduled session begins, in HH:MM 24-hour format (e.g., '08:00', '13:30').

attributes.name: slot_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Duration of each individual appointment slot within the session, in minutes (e.g., 15, 30, 60). Determines how many slots are generated per session.

attributes.name: source_system

attributes.name: source_system_code

attributes.name: telehealth_enabled_flag

attributes.name: template_name

attributes.name: template_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the schedule template. Active templates are used for slot generation; inactive/retired templates are historical.

attributes.name: template_type
attributes.description: Classification of the schedule template indicating whether it applies to a provider, resource, facility, equipment, room, or staff member.

attributes.name: waitlist_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a waitlist is maintained for this schedule template when all slots are filled. True enables waitlist management; False does not.

products.name: open_slot
products.description: Individual available scheduling slots generated from schedule templates for providers, rooms, and equipment. Captures slot date/time, duration, slot type, care setting, resource assignment, appointment type eligibility, hold status, and remaining capacity. Represents the real-time inventory of bookable time — aligns with HL7 FHIR Slot resource. Consumed by appointment booking workflows, patient self-scheduling (Epic MyChart), and patient access teams in Epic Cadence and Cerner scheduling.
products.reference: Epic Cadence Slot / HL7 FHIR Slot Resource

attributes.name: open_slot_id

attributes.name: care_site_id

attributes.name: clinician_id

attributes.description: Reference to the parent schedule template from which this slot was generated. Links to the schedule data product that defines recurring availability patterns for providers, rooms, or equipment.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to facility.service. Business justification: Open slots are offered under specific clinical services for referral routing and patient self-scheduling. Service-level slot availability reporting and access metrics (e.g., third-next-available appoi

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to provider.specialty. Business justification: Slot availability by specialty drives patient self-scheduling, network adequacy gap analysis, and provider directory accuracy. specialty is a denormalized text representation of the specialty entity;

attributes.name: appointment_type_eligibility
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of appointment types that are eligible to be booked in this slot. Examples include new patient, follow-up, annual physical, procedure. Enforces business rules for slot utilization.

attributes.name: block_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation for why the slot is blocked or unavailable. Examples include provider time off, equipment maintenance, facility closure, administrative time. Null if slot is available for booking.

attributes.name: block_type
attributes.description: Categorization of the reason the slot is blocked. Used for reporting on non-clinical time utilization and capacity planning. Null if slot is not blocked.

attributes.name: care_setting
attributes.description: The care delivery environment where the slot is available. Distinguishes between outpatient clinics, inpatient units, emergency department (ED), operating room (OR), telehealth, and home health settings.

attributes.name: comment
attributes.description: Free-text notes or special instructions associated with the slot. May include preparation requirements, patient instructions, or scheduling coordinator notes. Visible to scheduling staff and potentially to patients.

attributes.name: created_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when this slot record was first created in the scheduling system. Used for audit trail and slot generation tracking.

attributes.name: hold_expiration_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when a held slot will automatically be released if not confirmed. Null if slot is not currently held. Used to prevent indefinite slot blocking and optimize capacity utilization.

attributes.name: hold_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation for why the slot is held. Examples include pending insurance authorization, awaiting patient callback, reserved for urgent referral. Null if slot is not held.

attributes.name: hold_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the slot is currently held for a specific patient or referral. Held slots are temporarily reserved pending confirmation. Expired holds are automatically released after a configured timeout period.

attributes.name: insurance_eligibility
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of insurance types or payer groups accepted for this slot. Examples include Medicare, Medicaid, commercial, self-pay. Used for payer-specific access management and network compliance.

attributes.name: last_modified_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when this slot record was last updated. Tracks changes to slot status, capacity, or configuration. Critical for real-time slot availability synchronization.

attributes.name: max_capacity
attributes.description: The maximum number of appointments that can be booked in this slot. Typically 1 for individual provider appointments, but may be higher for group visits, classes, or high-volume clinics.

attributes.name: online_booking_cutoff_hours
attributes.description: The minimum number of hours in advance that a patient must book this slot online. Prevents same-day or last-minute online bookings. Null if no cutoff applies or online booking is disabled.

attributes.name: online_booking_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this slot is available for patient self-scheduling through online portals such as Epic MyChart or Cerner patient portal. False restricts booking to staff-assisted scheduling only.

attributes.name: overbook_allowed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this slot can be overbooked beyond its max_capacity. True allows scheduling additional appointments when slot is full, typically used for urgent or walk-in patients. False enforces strict capacity limits.

attributes.name: patient_type_eligibility
attributes.description: Defines which patient types can book this slot. Examples include established patient only, new patient only, pediatric, adult, geriatric. Used to enforce age restrictions and patient relationship requirements.

attributes.name: remaining_capacity
attributes.description: The number of appointments that can still be booked in this slot. Supports overbooking scenarios where multiple patients can be scheduled in the same time slot. Value of 0 indicates slot is fully booked.

attributes.name: slot_category
attributes.description: Broad categorization of the slot for grouping and filtering purposes. Examples include outpatient, surgical, diagnostic, telehealth, emergency. Used for capacity planning and reporting.

attributes.name: slot_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The length of the slot in minutes, calculated as the difference between slot_end_datetime and slot_start_datetime. Standard durations vary by appointment type and provider specialty.
attributes.references: Derived from HL7 FHIR Slot.start and Slot.end

attributes.name: slot_end_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the slot ends. Represents the latest time an appointment can conclude in this slot. Used to calculate slot duration and prevent overbooking.

attributes.name: slot_identifier
attributes.description: Human-readable business identifier for the slot, typically generated from schedule template and date/time. Used for external reference and display in Epic Cadence and Cerner scheduling interfaces.

attributes.name: slot_start_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the slot begins. Represents the earliest time an appointment can start in this slot. Critical for patient scheduling and resource allocation.

attributes.name: slot_status
attributes.description: Current availability status of the slot. Free indicates bookable, busy indicates occupied, busy-unavailable indicates blocked, busy-tentative indicates held pending confirmation. Aligns with HL7 FHIR SlotStatus value set.

attributes.name: slot_type
attributes.description: Classification of the slot indicating the kind of appointment or service that can be booked. Examples include new patient visit, follow-up, procedure, telehealth, walk-in. Sourced from Epic Cadence visit type or Cerner appointment type configuration.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this slot was sourced. Examples include Epic Cadence for outpatient scheduling, OpTime for surgical scheduling, Cerner scheduling for inpatient appointments.

attributes.name: source_system_identifier
attributes.description: The unique identifier for this slot in the source operational system. Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and bidirectional synchronization between lakehouse and operational systems.

attributes.name: waitlist_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether patients can be added to a waitlist for this slot if it is fully booked. True enables waitlist management for high-demand slots. Used for cancellation backfill and access optimization.

products.name: surgical_case
products.description: Master record for every scheduled surgical or procedural case managed through OpTime or Cerner SurgiNet. Captures case type, procedure codes (CPT/ICD-10-PCS), scheduled OR suite, primary surgeon, anesthesia type, estimated duration, case status (requested, scheduled, in-progress, completed, cancelled), ASA classification, and block time utilization. SSOT for surgical scheduling distinct from outpatient appointments.

attributes.name: case_type

attributes.name: consent_obtained_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether informed consent has been obtained from the patient or legal representative. Required before proceeding with surgery. Used for compliance verification.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission Surgical Standards, HIPAA Authorization Requirements

attributes.name: consent_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when informed consent was obtained. Used for regulatory compliance documentation and pre-operative checklist verification.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the surgical case record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: equipment_requirements
attributes.description: Special equipment or instrumentation required for the surgical case. Free-text or structured list of equipment codes. Used for equipment scheduling and availability verification.

attributes.name: estimated_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Estimated length of the surgical procedure in minutes. Based on historical averages for the procedure type, surgeon, and patient complexity. Used for block time allocation and scheduling optimization.

attributes.name: facility_code

attributes.name: implant_required

attributes.references: FDA Unique Device Identification (UDI) System, Epic Supply Chain Integration

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the surgical case record was last updated. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data quality monitoring.
attributes.references: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.312, Epic Audit Log

attributes.name: laterality
attributes.description: Anatomical side on which the procedure is performed. Critical for surgical site verification and wrong-site surgery prevention. Part of the Universal Protocol.

attributes.name: patient_class
attributes.description: Patient classification for the surgical encounter. Determines billing rules, bed assignment requirements, and post-operative care pathways.
attributes.references: CMS Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS), CMS Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS)

attributes.name: post_op_diagnosis

attributes.name: requires_blood_products

attributes.name: requires_icu_bed

attributes.description: Indicates whether the patient will require an ICU bed post-operatively. Used for bed management and capacity planning coordination between OR and ICU.

attributes.name: scheduled_date
attributes.description: Date on which the surgical procedure is scheduled to occur. Used for day-level capacity planning and patient preparation scheduling.

attributes.name: scheduled_end_time
attributes.description: Anticipated date and time when the surgical case is expected to conclude. Calculated from scheduled start time plus estimated duration. Used for downstream resource planning.
attributes.references: Epic OpTime Duration Calculation, OR Turnover Planning

attributes.name: scheduled_start_time
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the surgical case is scheduled to begin. Used for minute-level OR scheduling, staff coordination, and patient arrival instructions.

attributes.name: site_marked_indicator

attributes.references: The Joint Commission Universal Protocol, WHO Surgical Safety Checklist

attributes.name: timeout_completed_indicator

attributes.references: The Joint Commission Universal Protocol, WHO Surgical Safety Checklist

attributes.name: urgency_level

attributes.description: The portion of total charges that are not covered by the patient's insurance plan. Represents charges that are patient responsibility or not eligible for payer reimbursement.

attributes.name: outstanding_balance
attributes.description: The remaining unpaid balance on this invoice after all payments and adjustments. Represents the current amount due from all responsible parties.

attributes.name: patient_payment
attributes.description: The total amount paid by the patient toward this invoice. Sum of all patient payments including copays collected at time of service and subsequent patient payments.

attributes.name: patient_responsibility
attributes.description: The total amount the patient is responsible to pay, including deductibles, copayments, coinsurance, and non-covered charges. Calculated after insurance adjudication.

attributes.name: place_of_service_code
attributes.description: Two-digit code on CMS-1500 professional claims identifying the location where services were rendered. Examples: 11=Office, 21=Inpatient Hospital, 22=Outpatient Hospital, 23=Emergency Room.

attributes.name: revenue_code

attributes.name: service_from_date
attributes.description: The start date of the service period covered by this invoice. For single-day encounters, equals service_through_date. For multi-day stays, represents admission or first service date.

attributes.name: service_through_date
attributes.description: The end date of the service period covered by this invoice. For single-day encounters, equals service_from_date. For multi-day stays, represents discharge or last service date.

attributes.name: statement_date
attributes.description: The date a patient statement was generated and sent for this invoice. Tracks patient billing communication in the revenue cycle.

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: The date the invoice was submitted to the payer as a claim. Represents when the billing document was transmitted electronically or mailed to the insurance company.

attributes.name: submission_method
attributes.description: The method used to submit the claim to the payer. Electronic 837 transactions are the standard for HIPAA-compliant electronic claims submission.

attributes.name: total_charges
attributes.description: The total gross charges for all services on this invoice before any adjustments, discounts, or payments. Sum of all charge line items from the Charge Description Master (CDM).

Supports both CMS-1500 and UB-04 line-level detail.

products.name: coding_assignment
products.description: Clinical coding record associating ICD-10 diagnosis codes, CPT procedure codes, DRG assignments, HCPCS codes, and CDI query workflows to a specific encounter or invoice. Owns principal and secondary diagnoses, principal and secondary procedures, DRG code, DRG description, DRG type (MS-DRG, APR-DRG), DRG weight, MDC (Major Diagnostic Category), geometric/arithmetic mean LOS, outlier threshold, expected reimbursement, grouper version, assignment date, coder ID, coding method (auto/manual), coding date, and CDI query data (query type — compliant/leading/non-leading, query topic, query date, response deadline, response date, physician response — agree/disagree/no response, resulting code change, DRG impact amount). Managed via 3M HIS DRG grouper, 3M CDI, and Epic HIM module. SSOT for all coded encounter data, DRG assignment, and CDI query tracking — there are no separate DRG or CDI entities. Supports CMI (Case Mix Index) reporting, DRG-based reimbursement calculation, and CDI program performance measurement.

products.name: coverage
products.description: Insurance coverage record linking a patient to a specific payer plan for a defined benefit period, including the complete history of real-time and batch eligibility verification transactions. Owns payer ID, plan name, plan type (HMO, PPO, POS, Medicare, Medicaid), member ID, group number, subscriber ID, subscriber relationship, coverage effective/termination dates, coordination of benefits (COB) order (primary/secondary/tertiary), copay amount, deductible amount, out-of-pocket maximum, and eligibility verification events (verification date, verification method — real-time 270/271, manual, batch — payer response status, coverage active flag, deductible met amount, out-of-pocket met amount, copay amount returned, verification source system). SSOT for patient insurance eligibility, coverage verification, benefit details, and all eligibility verification transactions — there is no separate eligibility check entity. Supports front-end revenue cycle eligibility workflows and reduces claim denials due to eligibility issues.

Owns plan type (standard, interest-free, hardship), total plan amount, installment amount, installment frequency, plan start date, plan end date, number of installments, installments paid, remaining balance, plan status (active, completed, defaulted, cancelled), and enrollment channel. Supports patient financial engagement and self-pay collections.

attributes.name: last_payment_date
attributes.description: Date when the most recent installment payment was received and posted.

attributes.name: number_of_installments
attributes.description: Total number of scheduled installment payments required to complete the payment plan.

attributes.description: Total outstanding patient balance at the time the payment plan was established. This is the starting principal amount before any plan payments are applied. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: payment_method
attributes.description: Primary payment instrument used for installment payments. Credit card and debit card indicate card-based payments, ACH (Automated Clearing House) indicates electronic bank transfer, check indicates paper check, cash indicates in-person cash payment, and money order indicates certified payment instrument.

attributes.name: plan_number

attributes.name: plan_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the payment plan.
